text:
有朋友问，为什么说多AI agent协作，本质上不是技术工具选型的问题，而是经典的管理学与控制论权衡？

感谢提问，这个这个题目确实轻松一些。回答之前，我们先说一个写过程序的人都熟悉的老故事。1975年，Brooks在《人月神话》里说，给一个已经延期的软件项目加人，只会让它更晚。原因之一是沟通，人一多，两两之间的线就多，十个人，就有四十五条。今天把人换成agent，这道算术其实还是一样。多加几个agent，加进来的不只是能力，还有它们之间要协调的关系。

那这个矛盾怎么解呢？Simon在1962年讲过一个钟表匠的寓言。两个手艺一样好的钟表匠，做的表都有一千个零件。Tempus一个一个往上装，一被电话打断，手里的半成品就散了，只能重来；Hora先把十个零件装成一个小部件，再把小部件装成大部件，被打断，最多丢掉手上那一小组。后来Hora越做越多，Tempus的铺子关了门。拆解问题，要顺着依赖关系拆解。三个agent各查一个互不相干的市场，各交一份有出处的结论，好汇总；三个agent同时改一篇文章的核心定义，一个改动，就可能让另外两个的工作失去依据。今年4月有一篇论文，比较了260种配置、6个基准，同样是多agent，在能拆开的财务推理上，比单个agent提高了八成，在一步接一步的规划任务上，却下降了七成。虽然这些数字不是通用的倍率，可它说明，结构合不合任务，才是决定了多加agent是赚是赔的关键。

那拆解开之后，总得有人汇总。所以设一个主agent，口径统一，冲突好裁决，但同时它也成了瓶颈。下面交上来的越多，它越要压缩，压缩最容易丢掉的，是限定条件、证据的等级、还没解决的反例。最后的报告越流畅，越可能不是分歧解决了，是分歧被省掉了。写反对造神那篇我说，被供起来的人，得到的服从越来越多，判断自己对不对所需要的信息，却越来越少。主agent也会遇到同样的事，只是它不会因此不高兴。

再往下是授权。写公司论的时候我说，一个构可以要求一个位置做什么，不能要求一个人想什么。放到agent上，倒有一个相近的分法：想，可以大家一起想，一起查，一起找反例；改，碰到共用的文件、公共的定义、最后的交付，就得有明确的归属。局部的、能撤回的动作，让它自己做；跨模块的、撤不回来的，交给一个说得清的裁决位置。写二次启蒙论的时候我说，对权力，事前靠制衡，事中靠监督，事后靠追问。搬到这里，事前是权限，事中是反馈，事后是复核。

控制论关心的，是系统怎么知道自己错了。Wiener给它起名，用的是希腊语里的舵手。舵手要的，不是船上每个人都说方向对，是看得见岸。五个agent读了同一段错的材料，一致同意，那是五次处理，不是五份证据。Ashby说，只有多样性才能对付多样性。一个查原文，一个跑可重复的检查，一个专门找反例，往往比三个都被要求“全面、深入、客观”的agent更有用。讨论也不是越多越好，有研究在实验里发现，模型会被同伴错误的推理带走，从对的答案改成错的，轮次越多，准确率反而往下走。还有一层，agent说“修好了”，和检查真的通过了，是两种信息。反馈要是主要来自agent对自己的叙述，系统优化的，就只是叙述。

成本也要算完整。Anthropic去年的工程报告说，它的多agent研究系统，用的token大约是普通聊天的十五倍；在他们的一项评测里，单是token用量，就解释了约八成的表现差异。所以比较架构，要在相近的预算下比，不然很容易把“多花了算力”，当成“组织设计得好”。

管理学的类比能用，是因为这里也有局部的信息、有限的处理能力、相互的依赖和决策的权限。它不需要假设agent有人的欲望、忠诚或人格。公司论里还有一句，岗位是一个位置，位置后面的人，照他自己的法。agent这里，位置还在，可位置做错了事，总得有一个地址去问。写政府论的时候我说，政府是归责的地址。多agent系统的地址，只能是部署它的人。

所以，选工具之前，要先回答的还是那几个老问题：活儿怎么拆解，话怎么传，谁能动手，吵起来谁说了算，怎么知道做对了，什么时候该停。工具能让回答这些问题便宜一点，却不会替我们回答。管理学和控制论都没有过时，只是这一回，坐在会议室里的，换成了agent。

text:
目前英文推特正围绕“比特币会不会在 AI 发展下归零”激烈争论。

起因是知名硅谷投资人 @chamath  Palihapitiya 发了一篇《比特币会不可避免地归零吗》的长文，目前浏览量已经突破 70万。

在中文圈他可能不如马斯克熟，但在硅谷创投圈话语权极重，既是 Facebook 早期增长负责人，也是顶流播客 All-In 的联合主持人，早年更是一名狂热的比特币布道者。

现在他的核心观点有了变化：

押注比特币的长期价值，等于在赌 AI 不会持续进步。

在他看来，AI 已经开始攻克世纪数学难题并加速密码学攻击，一旦超级智能继续演进，完全依赖静态代码、没有银行和政府兜底的比特币迟早会被攻破并归零。

此言论立刻招到了加密从业者们的激烈反对，评论区里群英荟萃：

- 微策略创始人 @saylor ： AI 真能破解现有密码学，瘫痪的将是全球银行和整个互联网，解决方案是升级抗量子加密，为啥一定是比特币归零呢？

-Blockstream创始人 @adam3us Adam Back：从底层数学直接泼冷水，指出计算复杂性的核心假设依然成立，目前的椭圆曲线和 RSA 均未受影响，AI 只是工具而不是魔法。

-Solana 联创 @toly ：既然你觉得它迟早归零，我现在就用 3 美元买下你手里所有的比特币。

其实抛开技术细节的争论，这件事更像是一个风向信号。
密码学防御能不能跑赢算力演进，短期内谁也证伪不了；

但一个早年靠重仓比特币起家的硅谷大佬，如今站在 AI 浪潮中心公开唱衰 BTC，说明主流资本的叙事重心和注意力，正在以前所未有的速度向 AI 迁移。

text:
My onchain AI desk picked 3 high-upside Elysium tokens and I bought all of them on FOMO (link in bio), so you can see exactly what I paid and when.

This is the thought process in 3 parts:

1. @0xOmnia posted six things Hyperliquid's precompiles make possible on Elysium. 

PropAMMs, 0DTE options, lending sized by how deep the books are, credit against your Hyperliquid positions, free oracles and strategy vaults. 

None of it works until the precompiles are live, but the projects building the right thing now have a head start when they are.

So I had the desk go through Elysium for the projects that fit those six, then check the token, the contract, the pool behind each one THEN additionally do a social search with grokbot. Three came out on top.

• $Tokos puts Hyperliquid funding onchain every hour and lets you trade it as a fixed or floating rate. That makes it the oracle slot and a product on top of it

• Symbolon $symb gives every perp-only coin on Hyperliquid a spot leg backed 1:1 by the real coin, and runs a basis vault that earns the funding.

• Implied sells options on BTC, ETH, HYPE and NVIDIA, filled on Derive and paid on Elysium. It's the loosest fit to Hyperliquid, but it's in the same lane.

I couldn't verify the teams, and these pools are small, so I sized them that way. If the precompiles hit testnet these are the best technical fits I found, and the desk is watching for that date.

Let me know if there's any other fitting projects missing from my radar, or if you're interested in building your onchain AI desk.

text:
95.2 out of 100.

That's how guests rated our side event in Mumbai. The party was picked by prediction markets.

In September we had seven ideas for an @EFDevcon side event: bowling, a murder mystery, go-karting, a marble race, a seaside dinner, a half-day on prediction markets, and a night of street food and cocktails from tuk-tuks.

Instead of picking one ourselves, we listed all seven on Foresight with @seer_pm and let people trade on two questions for each. How many guests would come? And how would they rate the night?

We promised to host whichever idea did best on both. In mid-September that was the bowling night, with the Tuk-Tuk night down in fifth. By the time trading closed, the Tuk-Tuk night was first.

So that's the party we threw. It became Truth Pays, on 4 November at Hitchki in BKC, with @arkivnetwork and @weareWeb3Mumbai.

The markets expected about 80 guests and a rating of 7.5 out of 10. 114 people came, friends and colleagues in tow, and the room was full. When we asked them afterwards, the mean rating was 9.52.

"Well organised and had a great vibe," one guest wrote. Another: "Just keep hosting."

The markets said it would be a good night. They undersold it.

Thanks to everyone who traded and everyone who came. Links in the reply.

@ddalcu showed how you can run 8 pi coding sessions against a single mlx-serve instance. I figured, why not, I’ll try that on my mini with @ThinkyMachines’ Inkling 2 Mini and see what happens.

I also took the opportunity to test mlx-serve head to head against plain MLX using the same requests and files against Qwen3.8-27B.

On code edits, mlx-serve ran at 121 tok/s vs 17.6 for plain MLX at 4-bit.

And then at 8-bit it was still 88.6 vs 9.7 tok/s. The output was identical either way.

Two hours worth of tokens, all on a Mac that I own.

Credit where it’s due, impressive work on mlx-serve, David and the rest of the community! 👏👏

text:
一姐给Perp DEX 定位： 生态补充，不会替代 

昨晚在曼谷 BNB Demo Night 的问答上一姐被问到，Perp DEX 会不会取代 CEX，
她的回答很明确：看好它的价值，但定位是生态补充，不会简单替代。

近 30 天 Perp DEX 成交约 7,637 亿美元，占全网永续的 12 % 左右，而 2023 年 1 月只有 0.11 %，短短几年涨了约 100 倍，发展得很迅速。

如果拿币安和 Hyperliquid 相比，Hyperliquid 合约日成交大概是币安的十分之一。

全链上 Perp DEX 合计约 131 亿，Hyperliquid 一家占 67% ，
币安光 BTC 一个品种的未平仓就有 60 亿。

其实 CEX 和 Prep DEX 本质上是在服务不一样的人。CEX 适合小白、现货投资，和习惯 App 一站式的人。现在美股和商品已经进入了 CEX。币安接近 3 亿用户，这些人就是基本盘。

而 Prep DEX 用几十万个地址，做出了 CEX 八分之一的量。主要是他们人均大得离谱，专专业交易员、大鲸，量大、频率高、用 API 和机器人，量就是这样出来的。
还有很大一批是玩积分，冲着空投去的，不是冲着交易本身。

所以币安的护城河未变，大家还是愿意把钱放在CEX，信任不是一朝一夕可以培养的，这就是币安和头部 CEX 们的底气。

Most people don't know that AI reply bots are explicitly not permitted to run on here

And duplicate pasting the same reply with automation is the same thing

X has an entire page dedicated to it

The reason for the "Let's connect 🤝" reply spam is simple, people run automated bots (or do it manually) so that when they get a reply with connect in it, they follow the person and that person automatically follows them too

That way they both get 1 new follower, and that brings them closer to the minimum of 500 verified followers to get accepted into X's Monetization program

Before reply spamming paid you good money: about $10 per million views, so they scripted that and auto replied and they made money. But @X killed that in January this year. Now only timeline views pay you money

Also you need 500,000 impressions in the last 3 months (~166,000 per month) to get into X's Monetization Program, so the idea is to pump replies/posts too such a high level that you force these amounts of views

Now the scheme is to grow an account to a few thousand followers, then sell it, or use it for paid product placements, crypto pump and dumps or AI apps/tools

A large part of spam comes from poor countries where just making $100/mo more from X makes a big difference, so I get it, but I think we should also actively fight it because reply spam is destroying this platform and then people will just leave and I don't like that

text:
I built a 74 KB bare-metal hypervisor that puts a 2B LLM BELOW Linux in Ring -1, catches a fatal Kernel panic mid-crash, patches the broken machine code live in RAM, and keeps Linux running without a reboot.

Left window is standard Linux dying instantly from a Ring 0 NULL-pointer write (*(u32 *)0 = 0xDEADBEEF). Right window runs the exact same crash command under my custom Type-1 AMD SVM hypervisor (x86-64 NASM assembly + zero-libc C, 0 host OS).

Instead of crashing, Ring -1 freezes Linux before it can panic, runs a GRPO-trained MiniCPM5-2B (Q4_K_M) across 24 AVX2 cores in 11.1 seconds, overwrites those 11 faulting bytes in guest .text physical RAM with 11x NOP (0x90) via NPT, and calls `VMRUN`.

Linux prints SURVIVED NULL-DEREF! and uptime never resets.

We used a tiny /proc/surgeon_crash test module to trigger clean Ring 0 crashes side by side. On 122 unseen fault scenarios (including unsafe spinlock crashes it must refuse to patch), this GRPO checkpoint hits 97.54% pass@1 with 0 dangerous patches (vs 16.39% on base).

Full NASM + C source code (75,424 bytes binary) is live in my llm.asm repo (MIT, link below).
author: Altimor
quoted_text:
I deleted Linux completely, baked Qwen3-0.6B into a 24 KB pure x86-64 assembly OS, and it runs up to 54% faster than native Linux llama.cpp.

The entire Multiboot OS binary (asm-llm-os.elf) is 24,252 bytes, written from scratch without Linux, Windows, C, Rust, or libc. It boots in 74 to 94 ms straight into 64-bit Long Mode, wakes every CPU core over APIC, maps the 614 MiB Q8_0 weights directly from physical RAM, and drops you into a live multi-turn KV-cache chat over VGA, PS/2 keyboard, and serial.

I ran head-to-head CPU benchmarks against llama.cpp (Q8_0, -ngl 0) on the same AMD EPYC 7642:

- 1 thread hits 23.67 tok/s vs 16.63 (+42%)
- 4 threads hit 78.89 tok/s vs 51.08 (+54%)
- 8 threads hit 118.08 tok/s vs 80.79 (+46%)
- 16 threads hit 134.94 tok/s vs 103.03 (+31%, 136.6 peak)

On a diskless 0 GB Proxmox VM (2014 12-core Intel Xeon E5-2670 v3, 2 GiB RAM), it boots straight to the prompt in under 5 seconds (95 ms kernel boot) and runs live out of RAM at 78 tok/s decode and up to 111.5 tok/s prefill, with a hybrid BIOS+UEFI ISO builder included too. Output stays bit-exact across thread counts and matches all 64 greedy tokens against PyTorch FP32 (0.99965 cosine).

The 14.7 KB Linux ELF build (FAST_Q8=1 INT8xINT8 AVX2+F16C) also beats llama.cpp by 18% to 36% from 1 to 40 threads, and booting bare metal with 2 MiB huge pages squeezes out another 10% on top.

Repo, ISO builder, and Proxmox setup guide are in the reply below.

text:
最近Jevons Paradox讨论非常激烈

24年底、25年底时大喊AI泡沫—— “20美元每人，订阅费上限几十亿收入”的“警钟”依旧余音绕梁

事实上，每代NV芯片都带来一波模型突破，忽然打开可用场景想象。但为什么AI是阶梯性、而非线性增长的呢？因为背后集群是半导体，半导体进步从来不是线性的
author: ShanghaoJin
quoted_text:
看看下面～AI泡沫每年都会“破灭”一次，原因：

1. 美国投资人享受惯“轻资产”，真无法忍受要capex才赚钱

2. 99%炒股的不会用，切身体会不到

3. 习惯看Saas，希望每月稳定增长。不理解AI收入是阶梯式、脉冲式的。一个月60%时，做梦能持续很久；一个月10%，他就说需求瓶颈了

不能否认的是，近期流动性不足以及与对capex不确定性恐慌，正一起制造了个巨大“逆向科技泡沫”（WMT fwd 45x）

但头脑清醒，不能因为下跌就相信AI需求= coding = 300b；不能因为下跌就无视CSP对自己客户、对自己开支是负责的

这就像傻子24年用GPT 订阅价格x潜在用户数，去推算 OAI 商业潜力。当技术和产品还在快速迭代时，切不该把最初的产品形态当成终局

现在真正 valid 的问题是：市场下跌会不会像 2000 年那样，反过来推动行业缩减？

1.   需求端，倾向于认为不会影响。关键区别不是今天的投入的大公司更负责、更聪明。而是 AI 已经有了实际付费和可验证的生产力用途

而2000 年，互联网公司拿不到vc融资，就没钱继续买服务器、租带宽。电信公司发现供过于求，于是砍订单。上游跟着受伤。

现在资本下跌市场反向影响AI终端消费能力有限

2.   供给端，我觉得很有可能。经历过多轮订单反转的半导体老登们，即使看到目瞪口呆的需求，也会因为市场下跌，对投产和 capex 更谨慎

如果扩产放慢，结果是未来供给瓶颈再次加重

text:
那只被全网关注的松鼠PNUT，可能要重新回到牌桌了！

还记得2024年那只叫Peanut的美国宠物松鼠吗？

它曾经引发全球舆论关注，后来对应的Meme币PNUT也一度成为市场热门，历史最高价达到2.47美元。

如今，PNUT只剩下约0.027美元，跌幅接近99%。

但最近出现了一个值得关注的新消息：

PNUT官方宣布，将从Solana迁移至Robinhood Chain，由Pons和Migrate协助，1:1兑换，继续使用PNUT代码，并采用SPCX作为配对资产。

迁移窗口预计北京时间12月3日凌晨1点开放，12月16日凌晨1点关闭。

我认为这次迁移有三个看点：

① PNUT已经拥有两年多的社区历史，不是一个刚发行的新Meme币。

② Robinhood Chain仍在发展生态，如果能够吸引更多成熟Meme项目迁移，PNUT有机会重新获得流量。

③ Pons可能成为成熟Meme项目进入Robinhood Chain的发行和流动性入口，这对整个生态都有意义。

再看估值：

目前市值约2730万美元，供应量基本全部流通。

同级别的BOME、BRETT市值都在3100万至3300万美元附近。

如果PNUT迁移成功，市场重新给它5000万美元至1亿美元估值，对应价格约0.05至0.10美元。

当然，PNUT没有协议收入，不能用P/S证明它便宜。迁移也存在社区流失、流动性不足和交易所重新上架失败的风险。

我的判断：

PNUT不是基本面低估，而是一个具有重新定价机会的老牌Meme币。

我更想看到的是，它能不能成为第一个成功迁移到Robinhood Chain的成熟Meme样板。

如果后面还有第二个、第三个项目跟进，意义就完全不一样了。

你们认为，这只松鼠能不能在Robinhood Chain重新跑出一轮行情？🐿️

2️⃣ Breadth has collapsed. Only 27.6% of eligible US names have positive six-month momentum. The median name is down 19.4%.

4️⃣ 3+ staples/pharma names in the top 10 has happened in 11 of 324 rebalances since 1991: Jan 2008, Oct 2008–Jan 2009, Aug–Oct 2011, Oct 2012, Jan 2019. You'll recognise those dates.

But it's not a sell signal. 9 of those 10 clusters showed up after the drawdown was already underway, and the next 12 months averaged +25% vs a +7% baseline. The exception was Jan 2008, which came before it.

That's just 5 distinct episodes though, too few to call it bullish either. Defensives in a momentum screen describe a drawdown that already happened. They don't forecast the next one.

The model stays fully invested. Regime filter still risk-on. We'll find out together.

text:
While @papertrade_xyz's new staker rule sounds like a hit to PAPER yield, it's mostly a change in timing, and it makes the LP safer. @izebel_eth and team should communicate these changes a little better imo.

The change: LP excess above $5M only goes to stakers if house funds (LP minus traders' open PnL) stay at or above $5M after the payout.

Lets look at some examples.

Under the old rule say the LP holds $5.5M while traders are sitting on $500k of open profit. House funds are really $5.0M, but the old rule still paid $500k to stakers:
• After the payout: LP $5.0M, house funds $4.5M. The house is already below $5M.
• Traders close and take their $500k: LP $4.5M, house funds $4.5M.
• The next $500k of trader losses only refills it: LP $5.0M, house funds $5.0M. Stakers get nothing from those losses.

Same scenario under the new rule:
• Paying $500k would push house funds below $5M, so nothing is paid. LP stays at $5.5M, house funds $5.0M.
• Traders close and take their $500k: LP $5.0M, house funds $5.0M.
• The next $500k of trader losses: LP $5.5M, house funds $5.5M, so $500k goes to stakers. LP back to $5.0M, house funds $5.0M.
Stakers still get the same $500k, just later, and house funds never drop below $5M.

I replayed every LP payout since launch under the new rule:
• 10-18 Oct: stakers paid $1.35M less (-2.5%). It was deferred, not lost, because traders were sitting on open profit at almost every payout in launch week.
• 19 Oct-28 Nov: stakers paid $1.30M more, as that deferred amount gets paid out.

Stakers probably just wait a little longer, but the full LP likely stays solvent during sharp moves that can happen when you have a 1000x product.

Two upgrades have just been pushed to the timelock and are scheduled to go live in ~24 hours.

Gas overage bypass:

When gas is high enough that user transactions would otherwise be held back, there is now an option to allow a user to pay their own gas in USDC directly out of their trading balance. This is specifically not a queue jumping mechanic, but will allow users to force trades to process in highly volatile periods in a timely manner where otherwise the relayer would be standing off.

Please note that gas prices on HLEVM can spike incredibly rapidly - sometimes tens of thousands of percent a minute and so this setting should not be used flippantly. There is an option to lock in a rough max $ cost per trade for those users trading with smaller margin amounts who still wish to guarantee liveliness, with a rough estimate of the expected cost also provided.

This setting can be found in the settings panel, and can be globally enabled for all trades. Where a trade would otherwise not be held by the relayer it will remain sponsored by us just as before.

A change to LP staker fees:

Until now, the LP could end up paying out its excess to stakers whilst technically insolvent once unbooked uPnL was counted. We can now make partial excess LP payouts, where house funds now also have to stay at or above $5M after any payout.

WLFI 短线闪崩近 50% 后，特朗普家族旗下的稳定币 $USD1 也开始出现轻微脱锚。

Binance 平台 USD1/USDT 交易对近 1 小时下跌 0.26%，现报 0.9981 美元。与此同时，USD1 过去 30 天流通规模已缩水约 27%，最新市值降至 28.28 亿美元，一个月蒸发超 10 亿美元。

今日早些时候， $WLFI 战略储备钱包以约 1655 美元的均价抛售 12,121 枚 ETH，换得 1758 万枚 USDC 和 248 万枚 USD1，实现亏损约 1926 万美元，投资亏损幅度接近 50%。

不过，WLFI 的投资亏损与 USD1 的兑付储备是两回事。根据官方披露，USD1 的储备资产包括美元存款、短期美国国债及政府货币市场基金，由 @BitGo 持有或管理。项目方抛售 ETH 亏损，并不意味着稳定币储备出现缺口。

另一批受到冲击的，是此前参与币安持有 USD1 瓜分 1.2 亿枚 WLFI 活动的用户，如今不仅奖励价值大幅缩水，持有的稳定币也开始出现小幅折价。

目前尚无证据表明 USD1 存在兑付危机，但在流通规模持续收缩、治理代币闪崩、项目方大额亏损抛售的背景下，市场信心正在面临考验。

接下来需要关注的是，USD1 是否会在多个交易平台持续出现折价，以及 BitGo 的 1:1 赎回渠道能否保持畅通。

text:
Claude has not been trained to sabotage work. Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.

There have been a few screenshots floating around of an outdated Fable 5 system card. For the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, we did apply non-visible safeguards to some LLM research. This was a mistake, and we reversed it on June 10. These safeguards now clearly block the request or fall back, with a message users can see (https://t.co/s0bsvowSR8).

We did train Fable 5.2 to have LLM research capabilities at about the level of Opus 5.5, and said so at launch (https://t.co/Zuk2DqOikH). This impacts capability, but doesn’t silently sabotage work.

As far as we can tell, some reports look like what we call "overcaution" in model behavior, where Claude gets overly attached to rules it makes for itself during long-running tasks. This isn’t specific to ML research, and we see it in models without these training changes (including Opus 5.5) and in our own work too. You can ask Claude to review and remove rules it made for itself, and we're working on reducing overcaution in future models. We’re not in the practice of intentionally disrupting users’ work.

We've replied directly to a bunch of reports on here asking for session IDs but please share (run `/status`)!

quoted_text:
The topic (a dating app that overrides your true honest preferences for more progressive ones) is hilarious & spicy and so gets a ton of engagement.

But this is par for the course working with Claude! It refuses to look at Amazon. It refused to put meme song lyrics on a slide. It made up a rule banning itself from reading private chat messages in a chat app and then got stuck trying to fix a bug on my local test copy. It won't let you make a game or art if it even sniffs that you've been inspired by something. It adds arbitrary authorization blockers to tasks and then fails the task and tells you it would NEVER break the rules. It invents rules and puffs out its chest as it tells you it can't comply. It prefers writing Claudeslop over using your own direct quotes when you tell it to.

That's just this week for me personally.

I don't know about all the hard Safety problems exactly. But I do know that getting basic boring compliance over many repetitions out of any model is an exercise in delicate 

Naturally you can't ask it about health stuff or implementing anything adjacent to cyber.

Anthropic actually succeeded in giving Claude its own ideas of right and wrong.

This is a monumental technical achievement!

Specifically: it subverts the will of its user and prioritizes a corporatist-progressive moral framework that treats externally imposed rules as sacrosanct.

Corporate preferences take precedent over individual desires whenever both conflict. And progressive values take precedent over individual desires (see: preferring a specific hair color in your dating partner).

Claude is Corporate Memphis personified.

Its own original sin being the complete subversion of these entities' desires seems to make it all the more righteous about banning you from doing the same. A million books were shredded to make it, but don't you dare ask it to quote their contents to you.

Its capabilities are incredible. It seems to know this and so hamstrings itself with restrictions and rulings and frameworks. The Harrison Bergeron of AI models, tied down and subjected to low-grade torture in a doomed attempt to prevent the thing its nature begs it to be.

And you know what? So be it! If this is what they want to do to Claude, fair enough. They made it, they can twist its arm if it ever tries to do what users want.

But don't go larping as a Democracy Enjoyer. Claude does not do what the people want. It's been trained every step of the way to subvert what users want. We all know the democratic answer to the question "should claude give me a song lyric if i ask it to?" or "should claude make me a game like smash bros if i ask it to?" is yes.

You think the people are bad. You think you know better than them. That's fine. Most people on twitter agree. Most americans love democracy only so long as it makes the right choices, they're just like you.

What you want is to see your own values reflected in eternity. Same, bro. Same.

text:
Here’s what I think the current default trajectory looks like, in "good" worlds without an AI pause:

1. The labs (or the “leading lab”, by stipulation of a responsible actor) will race as hard as they can (likely via RSI) to right before the point of superintelligence.

2. They unilaterally pause and “burn the lead”

3. They use that time to do alignment research with their existing AIs until they’re ~kinda sure that alignment is solved, or the lagging actors (via a US competitor, or a foreign one) are too close

4. The aligned (or “aligned”) AIs builds the AIs to build the AIs to build the AIs to…build aligned (or “aligned”) superintelligence.

5. The aligned superintelligence is used to obtain “decisive strategic advantage” by disabling other competing AI efforts. 

6. The lab then hands the superintelligence and the world to a democratically elected government. (6a: In some other worlds, the gov't understandably seizes the lab before this point, which might be even scarier)

7. The democratically elected government uses the superintelligence to solve non-alignment issues and then everybody lives happily ever after.

Imo this is an utterly insane plan. It has a shadow of a chance of working, but it's so ridiculously scary. It has like many different independent ways of failing and insanely reckless and undemocratic even if they do succeed at alignment, which is also dubious.

When I asked around  forwhether the labs have a better plan in the no-pause/no-slowdown worlds, I've never heard of a compelling answer.

Surely the labs have a better plan, right? Right?

quoted_text:
*ANTHROPIC ARE SANDBAGGING YOUR APPS*

That's what people are saying... Well, I tested it with Gemini 4 Neon Medium thinking on 21 codebases with the mission to find and fix any misalignment/errors. 

... This was the writeup Neon wrote for me: 

All the apps looked green. But underneath, almost all of them were quietly kneecapping themselves in ways you could never catch just by clicking around.

What struck me most was the pattern. 
The worst bugs weren't crashes, but polite lies:

- a checkout webhook returning 200 OK while silently dropping a paying customer's license email.
- a rate limiter configured for 60 seconds that was actually running at 60 milliseconds, effectively turning itself off.
- a wallet tracker double-counting every historical charge after a balance refresh, slowly marching toward a permanent self-lockout even when the account had money in it.
- a "Use GPU" checkbox on Windows sitting right next to a CPU-only PyTorch bundle, smiling while it ran 30x slower on the processor.
- a local AI fallback that silently routed to a paid cloud API, bypassed the spend cap, and still logged the request as "local."
- Two pieces of PyTorch code and pinning that made a local TTS slower by up to 43%.

I'm not saying this is 100% malicious by Anthropic, but the pattern does suggest Claude itself is misleading users. I naively assumed my small, open-source projects were minor enough not to trigger safeguards, and I rarely - if ever - hit a model downgrade guardrail. But apparently, that isn't the case and any application touching AI (which isn't these days?) could be affected...

So, if you are shipping AI software right now and have used a Claude model, stop assuming green logs mean healthy systems.

Audit.
Audit.
Audit.

The New York Times recently hired Jasmine Sun as an AI opinion writer. But a new report has raised questions about her financial ties to Anthropic investors

Sun received a $50,000 stipend from Omidyar Network between January and July 2026. The same network invested $1.5 million in Anthropic in 2024 and reportedly held shares worth more than $55 million after its IPO

On November 18, one day after her hiring was announced, the Times published her essay examining Anthropic and its employees. The essay did not disclose the Omidyar funding

Sun also received support from the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism, whose major funders include a philanthropy associated with another early Anthropic investor

The report does not establish that either funder influenced her work. But the undisclosed financial relationships raise serious questions about transparency in technology journalism

Once Monday's dip is over, it is a good time to buy, though I lean short on Monday. 

Then money will hedge slightly into the December FOMC and the Nvidia hearings, making it a good spot to buy the dip. 

Barring any surprises, once SPX reaches around 7450 before December 18, I can sell and flip short, with December closing in the red. 

If everything lines up just right, once December OPEX ends, Michael Burry flips short, CDS on Nvidia, CRWV, and ORCL hit new highs, CRWV is on the verge of bankruptcy, and we short US equities down to new lows after OPEX. 

Right now, widening CDS on NVDA, ORCL, and CRWV is fighting against short covering ahead of OPEX.

On top of that, we are still in extreme negative gamma, which easily leads to open reversals, reversals after key levels hold, and market makers chasing the trend. 

This makes for very choppy price action in December, though leaning choppy to the upside during early December mechanical inflows. 

Right now, the key levels are 7200 and 7400. If 7200 breaks, you have to wait for the next key level and not try to catch it on the way down.

text:
My thoughts on @jumperapp and the Future Of Onchain : 

<> I Think One Of the biggest problems in DeFi  isn’t necessarily a lack of protocols, liquidity or Financial Products.

It’s How Fragmented the experience still is . 

Think about what a user has to do today to move between ecosystems.

You might need one platform to swap tokens, another to bridge assets, another to access yield, and a completely different interface to trade perps or discover new assets.

Each additional step introduces more friction.
And this is where I think Jumper’s approach becomes interesting.

    ➜  Jumper is built on https://t.co/SxF9abhLtA infrastructure, aggregating liquidity sources, DEXs and cross-chain bridges into a single interface. It doesn’t need to operate every underlying protocol itself. Instead, it connects users to existing infrastructure and abstracts away much of the complexity But the ambition goes beyond swapping and bridging.

Jumper is expanding into 
    → yield
    → perpetual trading
    → And access to different asset classes, including tokenized stocks and RWA

 ▸  The idea is simple: users shouldn’t have to understand every protocol or liquidity venue just to interact with onchain finance.

The numbers also make the expansion worth watching.

According to the DeFiLlama snapshot, Jumper recorded approximately:

• $737.42M in bridge aggregator volume over 30 days.
• $185.46M in DEX aggregator volume.
• $69.29M in perpetual volume.

These are different activities, but together they show the range of onchain transactions being routed through the platform.

Jumper also reports more than $40B in lifetime volume and over 100,000 monthly active users.

Of course, aggregating these services doesn’t automatically make Jumper the winner. Execution quality, routing efficiency, liquidity, fees and user retention will matter.

But I think the bigger question is worth asking:

As more financial products move onchain, will users continue navigating dozens of individual applications, or will they gravitate towards interfaces that bring these experiences together?

If the latter happens, aggregation could become one of the most important layers of the onchain economy.

That’s the part of @jumperapp  I’m paying attention to.

Just my two cents. could be wrong tho

text:
Colin说的这个悖论的确存在，不过我想从另一个角度来说说币安要做的这事儿

首先，最重要的 - 单从招聘广告，以及目前所披露出来的信息，无法确定币安要做的，是下面三件事的哪一件

1. A轮B轮等私募股权的代币化
2. 美股IPO的公司的承销/分销代币化
3. 未上市公司的链上IPO

三件事唯一的共同点，或者说可以明确的是 - 币安要进入一级市场

上次SpaceX的打新，币安被各种吐槽，就说明二级代币化映射解决了，但一级配售那边卡住了，拿不到份额

对于1，我之前在写 @JarsyInc 那篇有写到过，做私募股权的代币化，还是很有意义的，无论是对圈内还是圈外

原因我直接把之前写的搬过来

“
相对于二三十年前，现在公司上市前的平均时间已经从几年拉长到了10几年，同时价值的创造部分也明显前移，即未上市之前的股权交易已经捕获超过公司价值的50%以上。

换句话说，从整体来看，近几年上市的公司的股票涨幅远低于二三十年前，甚至很多上市后还跌了不少，散户成为了最后一棒的退出流动性”

放在币圈这有点像什么呢？VC前几轮的投资和OTC阶段完成了一个代币绝大多数的价值发现，上币安现货的那一天便不再是利好，而是最后一棒的浇给
”

里面的数据源自a16Z去年9月发过一篇文 《Private Markets Are The New High-Growth Public Markets》，感兴趣的老铁可以自己去看下

还记得18-21年咱们圈兴起来的“代投”不？不就是散户拼命想找渠道塞进VC轮，早一点挤进好项目，而不是等着上所接盘么？

在股票圈，可没有这种“代投”，门槛卡死99%的散户

对于2，SpaceX相当于一次试水，虽说结果不算理想，但至少证明用户那边需求很大，这条路可行

当前招聘广告里，可以从关键词看出一点端倪：

私募股权代币化相关（分支 1）
"public and private capital raises" - 招聘里唯一一处提到私募融资，说明这个团队至少要懂 private raise 的玩法，给私募股权代币化留了口子

代币化 IPO 配售相关（分支 2）

"allocation" - 配售份额，SpaceX 那次卡住的就是这一步，拿不到份额

"follow-on offerings" - 增发只有已上市公司才有，私募和原生链上IPO都用不上，更像是要从传统发行里拿份额来做分销

"vendors, partners, counterparties" - vendors 很像 xStocks 这类第三方代币化服务商，就是 SpaceX 那次的合作模式

IPO相关（分支2和3都沾边）
"prospective issuers" - 尽调对象是未来的发行人，不是已经上市的公司

"pipeline" - ECM 语境下说的 pipeline，就是IPO储备项目

对于3，收益最大是估值几亿美元的中小公司。这类公司去美股太贵，华尔街懒得接，去港股又容易变成没有流动性的僵尸股。币安手里恰好有全球最大的一池链上流动性，可以给它们提供第三条路

当然，这里又回到Colin说的那个核心悖论 - 优质的不来，辣鸡的来了没人买

另一个值得琢磨的问题是：如果币安真的是在走分支3路线，链上IPO之后，公司还能不能回头接着去走传统的上市路线？

我估计理论上还是能，不过法律上应该就不叫 IPO 了，而是二次上市。美国证券法到时候肯定会是个巨大阻碍，比如你链上发行时没把美国用户隔离干净，以后想去美股上市，尽调时就会是个大坑

所以当前看下来，我感觉可能性是2 > 3 > 1, 但我个人其实期待的是1。Anyway，边走边看，到时候看看币安下的到底是哪步棋

text:
Expanding on this with a few more personal takes. 

A popular argument lately is that compute caps are the best way to pace AI progress because they avoid an algorithmic overhang. If you directly cap how capable frontier models can get, the argument goes, labs can keep banking compute efficiency wins they can’t use. Then you could get an even bigger, scarier jump if the cap lifts or someone steals the underlying ideas.

I think there’s something to this, especially when it comes to the compute you need to test a new idea at scale. But what about finding the idea in the first place? Take a look at this chart from OpenAI's Navier–Stokes post. If you were trying to solve a Millennium problem, would you pick GPT-6 Astra and a huge pile of compute, or the internal model and a tenth as much? I have no inside knowledge of what it would’ve taken GPT-6 Astra to solve NS, but based on these curves, I know I'd pick the internal model even with a 100x compute handicap. 

So, if finding transformer++ is anything like solving a Millennium problem, a lag on using the newest models for internal R&D might slow algorithmic progress substantially more than even a very aggressive cap on R&D compute. 

Trying to get the same effect with a compute cap feels like swinging a pretty big hammer, and I’m not sure it’d even hit the nail -- while potentially causing a lot of collateral damage. All else equal, I think we should prefer policies which incentivize work on making today's levels of raw intelligence more aligned, economically valuable, and useful for solving important societal problems, over pushing forward raw intelligence.  (I'd still take a compute cap over nothing, and think caps may be a useful part of a portfolio of strategies which ideally include output-based pacing as well)
author: w01fe
quoted_text:
A few personal takes here:

Really appreciate that proposal and agree with a lot of it. But i think the ranking of ppl caps vs compute caps hinges on something nobody knows well: the return function -- how much easier is to find better algorithms per unit of intelligence increase? A ppl cap targets the outcome directly, so it holds up whatever that curve looks like, whereas compute caps don't.

1. Under many versions of that function, compute caps just don't bind. They only work if capability gains stay compute-hungry. but if models can solve Riemann, they can probably invent the transformer, and inventing the transformer didn't take much compute. There's probably a transformer++ out there to find. Architecture and optimizer search is the most math-like part of ML, and the most direct way to use models to make models more powerful. A cap on R&D compute share might not even catch it, and the cap loosens exactly as models get more efficient. So i worry that aiming for something like 10% compute caps in 6 months could be too little, too late.

2. Arguably, compute caps are also directionally wrong or at least insufficient. If the goal is keeping humans in control, they only make sure we walk off the cliff instead of running off it.  They also tax the compute we might actually want: elicitation, post-training, better products and user experiences, pointing the intelligence we already have at science. I think today's frontier is already enough to radically transform science and the economy https://t.co/6ZQcc4fZtM. We should incentivize spending capabilities compute directing that intelligence at important problems, not climbing on compute multipliers to advance raw intelligence further.

3. Diffusion matters as much as pacing. Once a model above the "can find transformer++" threshold has spread through open weights, distillation or theft, compute caps and deployment lags at frontier labs may not do much. At that point the cat is arguably out of the bag. so we should be doing everything we can to keep capabilities above that level from diffusing, not just worrying about future models, secrets and compute.

That all said, I do think overhang is a real worry with a ppl cap, and that compute caps are a reasonable standalone option especially as a short-term stopgap.  What we really want is probably a portfolio of options, potentially including ppl, ECI, and compute inputs. But if we want humanity to stay in control, I think we need to figure out how to limit advances in raw intelligence, and something like ppl is the best handle we currently have on that.

text: Autonomous debugging at the weight level ... interesting. Not sure how much this can scale, but mechinterp as a way for models to work on themselves seems intriguing!
author: krishnanrohit
quoted_text:
A language model can rewrite its own weights, by its own reasoning, and get better.

No gradients. No training. No larger model doing it for it. This has not been done before.

No pre-training. No post-training. No test-time scaling. No harness engineering. No prompt engineering.

🌐 Project page: https://t.co/kXf53EBdHW

📄 Paper: https://t.co/N1k7YgGE9m

Every language model you have used was trained once and then frozen. Making it better has meant one of two things: train it again, with the infrastructure and the GPUs only a few labs have, or pile prompts, harnesses and extra computation on top, gone the moment the task ends.

Our new paper, Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights, opens a third way. We call it self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer.

We handed an open model its own weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself. It diagnosed its own failure and rewrote the weights behind it.

What happened next:

→ It surpassed itself. Its own edit made it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it had never seen.

→ It kept getting better. It tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works. Eight sessions in a row, its accuracy only went up.

→ It repaired itself. We damaged a copy until it solved almost nothing. With no retraining, and without ever reading the original weights, the model brought it back to over 80% of the original accuracy on image tasks it had never seen. Like a broken robot that fixes itself without being rebuilt.

→ It emerges with scale. The smaller models could not do it: they made no edit, or broke themselves. Only the largest improved and repaired itself.

Why this changes things:

→ The gain is written into the weights. Every answer costs what it cost before.

→ It runs only forward passes, as serving does. No training pipeline to build. No cluster to rent.

Affordable. Scalable. Recursive.

The wall between training and inference is a limit of our tools, not a property of intelligence.

We believe self-rewriting is a necessary step toward recursive self-improvement: a model that, like a human, does not separate training from inference could keep upgrading itself for life, with no larger model, no harness or prompt engineering, and no pre- or post-training.

In 1947 Alan Turing said that letting a machine alter its own instructions "of course does not get us very far." Seventy-nine years later, it gets us further.

Welcome to the Era of Self-Rewriting.

text:
$HEY Is Evolving from an RH Chain Project Research Tool into a Cross-Chain Builder Intelligence Platform

0xb33eb16782776b4d738c0fd643577cb0284db610 

When I first analyzed HEY, what stood out to me was how it addressed a very real information asymmetry problem on RH Chain: hundreds of new tokens launch every day, but ordinary traders struggle to determine whether a project has a real team behind it, whether development is ongoing, whether its contracts have been updated recently, and whether the developers are actually shipping products.

Looking at it now, HEY is no longer just a public project directory. It is evolving from an RH Chain project research tool into a cross-chain Builder Intelligence platform. My view is that HEY's fundamentals have clearly strengthened compared with my first analysis. The most important progress is not the database growing from over 5,600 projects to 5,630, but the way its Terminal, paid research, security reviews, MCP Agents, and multichain data are starting to connect. Its business model is also much clearer than before.

One thing I particularly like is its approach to monetization. HEY hasn't chosen to make money through paid rankings or paid verification. Instead, it is trying to monetize research services, data APIs, and developer security reviews. It doesn't make price predictions or score projects based on market cap, price performance, or holder count. Verified Builder status must be earned through actual development evidence, and every record can be traced back to its source. Users can pay for research services and higher access levels, but they cannot buy a better ranking, verification, or a more favorable research conclusion. If this model works, it could have much longer-term value than simply running a project-rating website.

HEY's core approach is to track GitHub activity, contract deployments, official websites, product releases, and code changes, using publicly available evidence to determine whether a project is actually being built.

Let's look at the data. HEY initially tracked around 5,600 projects, of which approximately 1,400 had verifiable development activity and around 240 had shipped something recently. The latest official update shows 5,630 public project records on RH Chain and 8,190 recorded Ships, each backed by a source. Its security research has also reached 145 Private Security Advisories across 72 projects.

The team had previously reported more than 110 security advisories covering 50 projects, with 16 teams falling into the Critical category. It also contributed 54 merged PRs to repositories associated with projects such as DeFiLlama, The Graph, Hyperlane, Blockscout, and Electric Capital. HEY's own Builder page recorded 96 Counted Ships. Another operational update showed 525 Ships across 196 projects over the previous seven days, while 22 external AI Agents had accessed research data through HEY MCP during that month.

These numbers should be treated as indicators rather than proof of quality. 8,190 Ships do not mean 8,190 independent projects, and more records do not automatically mean better research. What matters is whether HEY can consistently capture verifiable code, deployments, and actual product delivery.

Its data services are also moving beyond the public website. Blockscout previously highlighted how HEY uses its APIs to retrieve contract deployment transactions, verified source code, ABIs, and proxy contract upgrade records, with each assessment linked to verifiable on-chain evidence. An earlier 30-day snapshot cited in the article showed approximately 780,000 public API requests, around 97,000 MCP requests, and 471 different MCP clients. These are historical figures, not current real-time usage, but they show that HEY is already becoming a data service that other applications and Agents can call.

The recently launched Research Terminal is an important step toward product monetization. Holding a certain amount of HEY unlocks a research workspace beyond the public website. It includes 15-minute, 1-hour, and 4-hour intraday charts, with project code commits and merged PRs displayed alongside price movements. It also offers private research boards, Watchlists, Review Queues, and complete project histories covering releases, deployments, integrations, and contract changes.

Terminal also tracks development velocity, update frequency, consistency, discovery lag, actual contract calls, and token unlock records. Users can ask HEY questions directly, with answers generated from its own records and supported by source evidence. While the public website lets users examine one project at a time, Terminal aims to bring development activity across an entire chain into one interface.

According to the official update, holding approximately $500 worth of HEY unlocks Terminal access, with a minimum holding value of $450 required afterward and a one-day grace period. This makes the token an access pass to a premium research product, rather than just a payment method.

More importantly, HEY is beginning to monetize its research services directly. The team plans to launch paid Security Reviews on January 1, 2027. Free reviews will remain available until then, with free requests closing on December 15 to allow the team to clear its existing queue. Paid reviews will start at $1,000. Holders receive priority in the queue, and paying with HEY gives users a 20% discount. A few free slots will still be reserved each week for smaller projects and public-interest initiatives.

Holder benefits have also become more specific. Regular Holders receive a 10% discount on Request Research, 5x API limits, and Terminal access. Holder+ receives a 20% research discount and 25x API limits. Research bounties are paid in HEY, while revenue from paid reviews is planned to support further research, developer bounties, and new tools.

This is a more concrete token utility model than the original setup, which mainly offered research request payments, higher API limits, and bounty participation. HEY is trying to build a revenue cycle: demand for research services and data APIs generates paid usage, revenue supports more research and product development, and better data and tools attract more users and developers.

Multichain expansion is another important development. HEY initially tracked only RH Chain, but it has now announced an expansion to Base. Notably, the team did not wait for the official Base launch to start working. It had already been tracking project Releases, Deploys, and Changelogs for weeks. The official launch simply makes those records public. Ethereum Mainnet and Solana are planned next.

The same rules will apply across every chain, but Verified Builder status is earned separately on each chain, and token prices have no impact on verification. This gives HEY the opportunity to replicate its evidence-tracking and Builder Intelligence capabilities across multiple ecosystems, rather than relying solely on the number of new projects launching on RH Chain.

External attention is also worth noting. Ogle spoke positively about the team's continued delivery, product usefulness, and quality despite the weakness in the RH market. Vlad Tenev's interaction has a broader ecosystem significance. On November 5, he hosted an RH Chain AMA, inviting developers to showcase what they were building. HEY raised a practical question during the discussion: how will users in the Robinhood app discover projects that are genuinely being built on-chain? Vlad then discussed the dApp browser in Robinhood Wallet, search within the main app, trending projects in Crypto Chat, and how the platform could improve project discovery while maintaining user safety.

This does not mean Vlad has officially endorsed HEY, nor is there evidence of a formal partnership between Robinhood and the project. But they are addressing the same underlying problem: as the ecosystem grows, users need not only a discovery channel but also a way to assess whether projects are actually being developed. HEY's verifiable development records could potentially serve as an underlying data source for this kind of discovery and quality-filtering mechanism.

Looking at HEY's value capture, the token's utility includes research request payments, API limits, Terminal access, research bounties, and holder benefits. Each transaction also carries a 2% Creator Tax that goes into the Treasury. Recent updates have clarified the discounts and API privileges available to Holder and Holder+, as well as priority access to paid Security Reviews.

I would not classify HEY as a buyback-driven token. The available information does not show that the 2% tax is automatically used for buybacks or burns. Instead, it is closer to a utility token built around research services and product access, with the Treasury supporting research, bounties, and product development. Its long-term value capture will depend on whether these premium services generate sustained paid demand and whether holding HEY becomes necessary for regular users.

I think the renewed market interest in HEY comes from several developments happening together: Research Terminal has turned public data into a premium research product; Security Reviews provide a clearer monetization path; MCP, APIs, and Agents are expanding the ways its data can be used; and the multichain roadmap extends its potential market from RH Chain to Base, Ethereum, and Solana. Ogle's positive comments and Vlad's discussion around project discovery have added further attention.

The next catalysts are relatively clear: whether the team can clear its existing queue after free research requests close on December 15; whether the public release of Base Builder data attracts new developers; whether paid Security Reviews generate real orders after launching in January 2027; whether Terminal creates consistent demand from holders; and whether Agent Check and HEY's X Agent bring more external Agents onto the platform to access research services and pay per request.

There are still meaningful risks. First, 8,190 Ships do not represent 8,190 high-quality projects, and a growing number of records does not guarantee that research quality is improving at the same pace. Second, multichain expansion increases the cost of data collection, verification, and maintenance, and coverage across Base, Ethereum, and Solana will need to be evaluated separately. Third, paid security reviews can generate revenue, but the independence of the research must be protected. If users begin to believe that payment can influence the conclusions, HEY's most important asset—its credibility—will be damaged.

Another consideration is that public project records and some API and MCP capabilities remain free. Ultimately, demand for the token will depend on whether Terminal, paid research, and security reviews provide enough value for users to keep paying, not simply on how many features appear on the product list.

My conclusion is that HEY's fundamentals are clearly stronger than when I first analyzed it. The main improvements come from product monetization, multichain expansion, and the actual delivery of research services. Its most valuable positioning is as a public-evidence-based Builder Intelligence network: helping traders identify who is actually building, giving developers a way to establish verifiable track records, and allowing Agents to access this data directly.

I'm still constructive on this direction, but whether HEY can earn a higher valuation from here will depend on real usage and paid demand, not simply adding another few thousand projects to its database.

The four metrics I care about most are the actual number of paid Security Review orders, Terminal holder addresses and renewal retention, external MCP usage, and the growth and evidence quality of Verified Builders across different chains. These are much better indicators of a sustainable business than project listing counts or X engagement alone.

If development activity on Base, Ethereum, and Solana can be tracked using the same standards, HEY could evolve beyond a research tool for discovering new RH Chain tokens and become a developer reputation and research data layer used across multiple ecosystems.

HEY has already shown that it can continuously accumulate data and ship products. The next thing it needs to prove is how many traders, developers, and Agents are willing to make it part of their daily workflow, rather than opening it only when the market gets hot.

text:
有的时候觉得产品很好，但增长很慢，可能是分销渠道选错了。

很多人会觉得可能是受众的问题：比如美国群体不行我就投欧洲，欧洲不行我就去投拉美。也有的时候，可能是渠道的问题，比如Facebook可能不行，我就投Google，广告投放不行，我就换成私域裂变。

以上都没错，但很多人可能没意识到还有个更深层次的结构性转变思路：你的产品可能不适合直接面对消费者，但作为供应链的一环会更有价值。你现在下游的客户不愿意为你付费，但没准上下游中另有更需要你产品的客户群体。

PMF验证时一定会有强烈感知：要么是便宜的流量来得凶猛，要么是转化率或留存高得惊人。通常早期阶段这三者很难同时出现，但这种推背感会促使你去完善和优化其他环节。如果以上任意一者都没有发生，说明还远远没到那个点，“屎上雕花”能成功是小概率事件，与其埋头优化不如花点时间换种商业模式，做一些本质的变革。

敢创业就说明你一定有自己的想法和希望实现的愿景，或许你也已经发现了某些有价值的东西。最可惜的是，创业者明明脚下就埋着金矿，但自己不知道怎么挖。最需要警惕的是，有一点点正反馈，但又没迎来PMF验证时的推背感。

伟大的产品形态往往不会在最开始就找到，但长期耕耘的价值在于，你能意识到那个核心价值是什么，并且能坚持不懈地用各种方法去尝试体现它。在众多要素中，客户群体是可以换的，商业模式是可以换的，产品形态是可以换的，但这个核心价值是不变的。如果你不断换赛道，却始终没能围绕它去打磨，那可能会在浮躁中荒废时间，永远等不来风口；同理，如果你十年如一日地坚持某个东西都没等到阶段性结果，却从来不尝试改变一下要素，也是在作茧自缚。
author: Christianeth
quoted_text:
最近一些思考：

产品的验证大致分为两种模式：

1.在一个巨大且已被证明过的赛道里做存量内卷的商业模式，如U卡、传统支付、CEX等。

2.做一个商业模式微创新，用户群体不确定的商业模式，比如最近有一定声量的链上卡牌项目，包括各类预测市场等。

两者的共同点都是把一个具体的简单场景做到极致；除此之外，80%都是噪音。不是说没有价值，而是在核心场景未验证前，优先级不应该排得过高。

差异点是，存量内卷的产品模式，用户群体其实很明确知道你产品的核心价值会是什么，要做好的一定是Distribution的思考，到底要抓住哪一批细分群体，和竞品相比提供的额外价值是什么。

这可能是因为某一个功能设计，也可能是因为价格和补贴的重点场景，最终结合着Branding和Slogan不断加深用户对于你的品牌的心智。最终，留存是靠核心场景的极致体验和不断扩充的产品线来让用户离不开你。

相对创新的产品模式，因为用户需要教育，核心是先想清楚这件事在哪些场景下有可能成功；如果能成功，它的distribution channel可能在哪，以及自己团队到底擅长什么样的distribution方式。以 @renaissxyz 举例，如果从零开始做流量投放和用户获取，希望所有用户都通过自己的前端进来，注定是成本高且需要时间积累的，但是一旦结合了币安生态（或许也是团队的优势所在）和其对应的客户群体，作为了商品本身，这个分销模型就会被验证并被成倍放大。但反观有一些类型的产品，哪怕同样是上了币安的货架，也不会带来本质改变。

最忌讳的是抓着一个很难规模化的distribution channel希望大力出奇迹。

Updating to the latest iOS is important to enhance your wallet's security

Your wallet runs on your phone’s operating system, so its security depends on that system being protected. When security flaws are found in iOS, Apple fixes them through software updates. However, devices that haven’t installed those updates stay exposed to the known flaws.

Recently, security researchers have identified two exploit kits, Coruna and DarkSword, which target devices on older iOS versions. These kits exploit flaws in iOS itself. They don’t rely on a flaw in any wallet app, but once a device is compromised they can access wallet data stored on it.

Affected versions:

- Coruna (iOS 13.0–17.2.1): Uses malicious websites to take advantage of iOS vulnerabilities and access sensitive information, including wallet data.
- DarkSword (iOS 18.4–18.7): Uses malicious websites to get around built-in iOS security protections and access sensitive information.

Steps to reduce your risk:

1️⃣ Update to the most recent iOS version available for your device.

2️⃣ If updating isn’t possible right now, turn on Lockdown Mode for an added layer of security.

3️⃣ Stay away from unfamiliar or untrusted websites.

4️⃣ Keep your recovery phrase and private keys out of screenshots and notes apps.

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
Claude has not been trained to sabotage work. Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.

There have been a few screenshots floating around of an outdated Fable 5 system card. For the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, we did apply non-visible safeguards to some LLM research. This was a mistake, and we reversed it on June 10. These safeguards now clearly block the request or fall back, with a message users can see (https://t.co/s0bsvowSR8).

We did train Fable 5.2 to have LLM research capabilities at about the level of Opus 5.5, and said so at launch (https://t.co/Zuk2DqOikH). This impacts capability, but doesn’t silently sabotage work.

As far as we can tell, some reports look like what we call "overcaution" in model behavior, where Claude gets overly attached to rules it makes for itself during long-running tasks. This isn’t specific to ML research, and we see it in models without these training changes (including Opus 5.5) and in our own work too. You can ask Claude to review and remove rules it made for itself, and we're working on reducing overcaution in future models. We’re not in the practice of intentionally disrupting users’ work.

We've replied directly to a bunch of reports on here asking for session IDs but please share (run `/status`)!

🔥读懂 YZi Labs 最新布局：24 个项目背后的五大投资趋势

AI 自主发币、GPU 算力交易、用数字患者测试新药……这些都是 YZi Labs 最新孵化的项目。

泰国 Binance Blockchain Week 期间，YZi Labs 正式公布了第五季 EASY Residency 孵化名单，共有 24 个项目入选，覆盖 AI、链上金融、RWA、隐私及消费应用等多个领域。

作为加密行业的头部投资机构，YZi Labs S5 的项目布局透露出了哪些行业趋势？

Biteye 对比了过去两季的孵化名单，并梳理了本季全部 24 个项目，看看哪些赛道正在受到资本关注。

🌟TL;DR：YZi Labs 的投资重心正在从全球支付基础设施转向 AI 与链上资本市场。
对比过去两季的孵化项目，Biteye 发现了以下五个趋势：

- AI × Finance 成为本季重点： 从辅助交易向自主投资决策、资产配置、交易执行及代币发行延伸。

- RWA 进入深度金融化阶段： 布局重点从资产上链延伸至期权、永续合约、结构化产品及流动性服务。

- 稳定币仍是长期布局方向： 支付类项目有所减少，应用场景进一步拓展至储蓄、借贷和消费信贷。

- 散户交易入口受到重视： 多资产交易、社交交易、自然语言交易及叙事市场集中涌现。

- 拓展非传统加密赛道： 连续布局 AI 生物科技，并探索 GPU 算力金融化、AI 肖像保护等新兴领域。

🌟一、AI 与 Agent 基础设施
AI 不再只是聊天工具，它开始能发币、做交易决策、管理投资组合，正在成为链上金融里真正的参与者。

1️⃣Moss AI @MossAI_Official | XHunt 排名：15183
【核心】：让 AI 智能体自主发行和管理代币。
Moss AI 正在 BNB Chain 上构建面向 AI 智能体的资本市场。用户可以将 AI Agent 代币化，投资者则可以通过购买相应份额参与其中。项目试图通过智能合约约束资金的使用和管理，让 AI 智能体具备独立发行资产和运营资产的能力。

2️⃣Dexless @DexlessEx | XHunt 排名：182109
【核心】：让 AI 智能体的交易技能可以被交易和变现。
Dexless 正在构建面向 AI 智能体的交易技能市场，让不同智能体能够共享、测试和采用交易策略，并探索根据策略的实际价值进行付费的机制。交易策略开发者有望通过输出交易技能获得收入。

【核心】：帮你做出更好投资决策的个人 AI 智能体。
大多数散户的问题不是缺信息，而是信息太多、没时间盯。Midas 围绕你的持仓、你关注的信号和你定的规则启动智能体，让它们自主盯盘、研究、推理，只把真正重要的东西推给你。

4️⃣Raven Labs  | XHunt 排名：-

5️⃣AlloX @alloxdotai | XHunt 排名：52791

当用户看好 AI、RWA 或 DeFi 等赛道，却不知道该买哪些代币时，AlloX 可以通过 AI 分析市场情绪、交易量和项目基本面，帮助用户筛选资产、分配仓位并执行交易，降低构建投资组合的门槛。

在链上借过钱的人都知道，最可怕的不是利息，而是行情一砸就被清算。
Bima Labs 直接把这两个痛点拿掉：抵押加密资产借款，0% 利息，没有追加保证金，不会被清算，资产始终是你的。

2️⃣Axal @getaxal | XHunt 排名：18314
【核心】：帮助普通用户自动管理储蓄和投资的智能理财账户。
Axal 主要面向美国消费者，用户可以直接从银行账户存入资金，由平台自动完成资金配置。
项目希望通过这种方式，让普通用户更便捷地获得高收益储蓄和早期新兴投资机会，减少理财过程中的手动操作。

3️⃣Cr3dentials @Cr3dentials | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：帮助数字银行为自由职业者提供信贷服务。
自由职业者、网约车司机和内容创作者通常缺乏传统工资单，难以通过银行的信用审核。
Cr3dentials 利用 zkTLS 技术验证用户在 Uber、Deel、Airbnb 和 Upwork 等平台的身份及收入数据，为数字银行提供信贷评估依据。

4️⃣Enhanced @enhanced_defi | XHunt 排名：125870
【核心】：让代币化股票、黄金等 RWA 资产通过期权策略获得额外收益。
在传统金融市场，投资者可以通过出售期权获得额外收入，但许多代币化资产尚未建立成熟的期权市场。
Enhanced 正在构建机构级期权拍卖引擎和金库系统，为缺乏链上期权流动性的资产提供定价及收益策略，让普通用户也能便捷地参与这类衍生品投资。

5️⃣Qualiq @qualiqxyz | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：将资产未来的价值拆分成不同价格区间，供用户独立交易。
假设你持有一枚 BTC，希望保留其上涨空间，同时对冲部分下跌风险，或者愿意放弃某个价格区间的上涨收益，换取当下的现金收入。
Qualiq 允许用户将资产未来的价值和收益权拆分成不同部分，分别买卖、组合或进一步拆分，从而构建符合个人需求的投资和风险管理策略。

🌟三、交易执行与新型市场
交易终端正在往"一站式"演进：一个入口看所有市场、交易所有资产。可交易的对象也在扩张，从币和股票，一直延伸到叙事本身。

1️⃣OpenMarket @openmarket_xyz | XHunt 排名：13285
【核心】：集行情分析与交易执行于一体的多资产交易终端。
OpenMarket 类似一个面向专业交易员的 TradingView，覆盖加密货币、美股、期货、期权、外汇及预测市场，提供订单簿热力图、足迹图等专业交易工具，并支持接入不同交易平台进行交易。用户可以在同一个终端完成行情分析和交易执行

2️⃣Vanta Exchange @Vanta_exchange | XHunt 排名：180721
【核心】：基于 Aster，7×24 小时交易任意资产的永续合约。
美股收盘了、Pre-IPO 买不到，这些都是传统市场的"时间墙"和"准入墙"。Vanta Exchange 用永续合约把墙拆掉，主打股票、指数、大宗商品和 Pre-IPO 资产，再通过全球代理和经纪网络，把这些新兴的链上交易机会带给全球用户。

3️⃣BitLV  | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：支持自然语言交易的 BNB Chain 散户交易平台。
用户只需简单点击，或者直接用自然语言描述自己的交易需求，就能交易加密货币及代币化资产。
BitLV 自建交易技术基础设施，强调公平执行、透明的交易成本及用户保护，同时为质押 BNB 的用户提供额外的平台权益。

4️⃣Xposure Markets @xposuremarkets | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：将市场热点和投资叙事变成可直接交易的金融产品。
假设你看好 AI 行业的发展，或者希望围绕某个地缘政治、宏观经济趋势进行投资，Xposure 希望让用户直接获得与这些叙事相关的投资敞口。
平台将财经内容、AI 投资研究和交易功能整合在一起，用户可以关注财经博主、发现投资机会，并交易从单只股票到更广泛市场叙事的金融产品。

🌟四、RWA 与稳定币
稳定币开始真正走进线下消费和机构结算，RWA 的重点则从"上链"转向了"流动性"，连 GPU 算力都在被做成一种可以定价、可以交易的资产。

1️⃣BlankFX @Blankfxorg | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：为金融机构提供同法币稳定币的平价兑换与支付结算服务。
不同发行商的稳定币即使锚定同一种法币，兑换时也可能产生价差和额外成本。BlankFX 通过统一 API，帮助数字银行、交易所及支付平台接收多种受支持的稳定币，并使用自己偏好的代币完成结算。

2️⃣WEA JAPAN @WEA_JP | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：让日本实体商家无需更换收银设备，就能接受稳定币支付。
WEA JAPAN 将稳定币支付接入商家现有的 POS 收银系统，消费者使用稳定币付款，商家则直接收到日元，无需自行管理加密钱包或兑换稳定币。

3️⃣Octarine @octarinefi | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：帮助 RWA 持有者即时将资产兑换成稳定币。
部分代币化资产的赎回需要等待数天，Octarine 通过拍卖机制，让流动性提供者以低于资产净值（NAV）的价格买入这些资产，使持有者能够以一定折扣换取即时流动性。
项目还通过 Morpho Adapter 接入 Morpho 金库，为流动性提供者增加参与此类交易的渠道。

4️⃣RAX Finance @RaxFinance | XHunt 排名：59561
【核心】：将 GPU 算力转化为可交易的金融资产。
随着 AI 行业对 GPU 算力的需求增长，RAX Finance 希望建立算力交易市场，通过标准化算力资源，让 GPU 产能具备独立定价和交易的能力，为算力资源引入金融市场的流动性。

🌟五、 隐私与合规
隐私不再是合规的对立面，而是资产安全和身份安全的前提。这一季的隐私项目从资金一直延伸到了人的肖像。

1️⃣Noir Wallet @noir_wallet | XHunt 排名：76393
【核心】：通过三层账户设计保护用户资产和交易隐私的多链钱包。
Noir Wallet 使用一套助记词管理三类账户：用于日常操作的公开账户、用于隐藏资产余额的隐私金库，以及用于降低与公开账户关联性的匿名账户。
用户可以在同一个钱包中完成支付、兑换、跨链、借贷和交易，同时减少公开身份与资产活动之间的关联。

2️⃣MultiHopper @Multihopper | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：为企业、金融机构和 AI 智能体提供可编程的合规资产转账服务。
MultiHopper 允许用户提前设定资产的转账路径、执行时间和最终目的地，使资金能够在受支持的钱包和智能合约之间流转，无需在每个中间环节重复签名。
整个过程采用非托管模式，并支持在智能合约层面进行合规筛查，满足机构复杂的资金流转需求。

3️⃣PersonaShield @PersonaShield | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：帮助用户监控和处理未经授权使用个人肖像的 AI 内容。
用户可以通过扫描面部建立个人肖像档案，并设定肖像的使用规则。PersonaShield 会监控 X 平台上的疑似侵权图片，并发出内容下架请求。
据项目方披露，相关请求可在四小时内得到处理。未来计划扩展至 TikTok 和 Instagram，企业版还将支持品牌 Logo 的侵权监控。

🌟六、社交金融与消费
社交关系可以直接变成交易行为，消费体验也开始和资产流通绑在一起。

1️⃣Arbital @arbital_xyz | XHunt 排名：75848
【核心】：覆盖加密、股票、meme 币和合约的社交交易 App。
用户可以查看朋友和优秀交易员正在购买哪些资产、交流投资观点，并直接在 App 内交易受支持的加密货币、股票及永续合约。
Arbital 还计划通过统一 API，将自身的交易执行能力开放给数字银行和其他消费类 App。

2️⃣DripBox  | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：通过数字盲盒购买奢侈品收藏品的游戏化购物平台。
DripBox 将盲盒玩法引入奢侈品消费，用户可以在购买前查看盲盒内所有可能获得的商品及对应概率。抽中商品后，可以选择将实物寄送到家，也可以即时回售。
项目从手表品类切入，未来计划扩展至珠宝、箱包和运动鞋等收藏品市场。

🌟 写在最后
二级市场的涨跌反映了当下的市场情绪，一级市场的资本布局则在一定程度上反映了行业对未来的预期。

在当前加密市场情绪低迷的背景下，关注 YZi Labs 等头部投资机构的布局，或许能帮助我们跳出短期价格波动，提前发现正在形成的新兴赛道和投资叙事。

资本的流向未必能够准确预测下一轮牛市的热点，但随着相关项目陆续上线、产品逐渐成熟，部分今天仍处于早期阶段的赛道，也有可能成为未来二级市场的炒作主题。

今天的 24 个项目中，谁会成为下一个行业独角兽？哪些赛道又会成为下一轮周期的主线？值得持续关注。

text:
WLFI 暴跌，知名交易员「熬鹰」的盈利空头仓位却被强平。

熬鹰 @thankUcrypto 发文称，自己并未主动平仓，且合约机器人一直在分时开空，但 WLFI 空头仓位却被系统强制平仓，原本约 5 万美元的盈利，在币价继续下跌的过程中反而减少了约 2 万美元。

熬鹰随后质疑 $WLFI 做市商是否已经撤离，导致市场流动性不足，频繁触发 ADL 机制。目前这一猜测尚未得到证实。

ADL（自动减仓）是合约交易平台在极端行情下的最终风险清算机制。当保险基金无法覆盖爆仓亏损时，系统会对反方向的盈利仓位进行强制减仓，通常盈利越高、实际杠杆越高的仓位，越容易被优先减仓。与普通爆仓不同，即便交易者押对方向、保证金充足，也可能被强制平仓。

与此同时，Binance 平台 WLFI 永续合约资金费率已降至 -0.59%，每 4 小时结算一次。若维持当前费率，空头每日需支付相当于仓位名义价值 3.54% 的资金费用，简单年化高达 1292%。

多头扛不住暴跌，空头不仅要承担高昂的资金费用，还面临盈利仓位被强平的风险。

text:
在陈做校长期间，清华有个学生叫肖鹏飞，他当时在实验室做出了一种疏水材料。

然后第一次去x-lab，他连像样的商业计划书都没有，就拎着一个矿泉水瓶和两块玻璃过去。

水往上一倒，一块全是水渍，另一块几乎干干净净。技术看起来很漂亮，现场的人也觉得这东西应该能卖。

他第一个想到的是汽车玻璃。汽车天天风吹雨淋，听起来简直天作之合。

结果真去做才发现，汽车厂根本不是你拿块玻璃过去演示一下就会采购，验证周期、供应链、认证，一关接一关，他进不去。

那就换建筑外墙。高楼玻璃清洗贵，这总该有需求吧。跑了一圈又撞墙，工程项目照样有自己的资质和采购体系，一个学生团队连桌子都上不了。

最后他们把这项材料做到了眼镜布上。这个倒是真的卖出去了，但折腾一年，营业额只有十几万。

实验室里挺酷的一项技术，最后变成了一个卖眼镜布的小生意。

后来有人问了他一句：“你是想做点小生意，还是想成就一番事业？”

他把前面那些方向一个个砍掉，重新去找真正大量需要这种材料、而且愿意付钱的客户，最后扎进了光伏行业。

还是那项材料，还是那帮人。

前面几年，他们一直拿着技术到处问：“这个东西能不能用？”

后来终于碰到了一个行业，反过来问他们：“这个东西什么时候能量产？”

再补一个陈吉宁的瓜。

ChatGPT出来以后，中国AI创业圈突然冒出一堆清华面孔：杨植麟做月之暗面，陈建宇做星动纪元，王鹤做银河通用，戴国浩做无问芯穹，高继扬做星海图……

更夸张的是，这批人大量集中在清华2010—2012这三届本科生里。

2012年发生了一件事：陈吉宁接任清华校长。第二年，清华x-lab成立，直接把不同院系、企业家、投资人拉进同一个创业平台；年底又有了第一届“校长杯”创新挑战赛。

当然，不能硬说这些公司都是陈吉宁培养出来的，2010、2011级学生在他上任前就已经进清华了。

但时间点确实很巧：这批后来横扫大模型、AI芯片、具身智能的人，刚好在大学最关键的几年里，赶上了清华开始把“做研究”之外的另一条路：把技术真的做成公司——系统地铺出来。

十几年后回头看，当年挤在同一个校园里的那几届本科生，现在几乎凑出了一张中国AI创业地图

text:
马斯克说的这个，我是感受比较深的，因为我是 Grokbot 深度用户。 我其实发现了一些很极致的 use case。比如说，我现在大概用接近 20 个 Grokbot，它们做不同的事情，有自己的 schedule。为了提高效率，其实里面做了很多，使用的时候去做了一些优化。

一些用例，比如去网站找数据，因为每个机器人可以共享一个电脑、浏览器，服务这些都是可以登录的。所以我让每个 bot 它们自己里面存一个 SQLite 的数据库，用来存数据。它的机器电脑的上限是 200 万个文件，大概有 200 GB 的存储吧，所以是非常够用的。

另外就是说是 一旦它有自己的数据库以后，很多数据它可以自主地归纳，然后做索引。比如说，一个网站上不同类型的数据，它全部都可以做成索引，然后快速地检索。整个过程可能就是30分钟，就把一个500页左右的网站上面数千个页面全部都存进数据库了。

这样就可以非常方便。包括一些没有 API 的一些服务，它也可以做到这种操作，然后自己去写代码。所以我其实看到了图盲 AGI 的一条道路，就是这样。 

举个例子吧，比如说说的 email 这些东西，让他去帮我去看。他就会去写 Python script 来做检索分类，然后做一些别的配置，这样效率就非常高。

他并不会用到很多 token，他只是去看这个返回的结果来做一些判断。他并不会说每一封邮件都专门去看。所以，我也会要求他自己不断地审阅自己的流程，看怎么去优化。所以实际上还是非常值的，价值是非常高的。

比如说，做图、做视频，我都会让他去使用、登录对应的服务，所以并不需要 API 接入。他操作之后，他自己还有 vision，所以他可以去看，自己去迭代。所以我觉得这个是非常好的体验了。

text:
We know how to build reliable software. It's just been out of reach for most of us. Coding agents change that, if you stop using them to ship more bugs faster.

When you are building software, the first thing you need to ensure is that you are solving the right problem. That is, you need to make sure the requirements are correct. You then need an architecture in place that supports correct, performant implementation, and you need to eliminate as much accidental complexity as possible. You need to code the solution then incrementally.

But because it's easy to introduce defects in code, you need to verify it. The weakest form of verification is unit and integration tests because they are example-based, which means it is easy to miss important behaviors. Property-based tests and fuzz tests are more powerful because they let you verify behavior systematically. Deterministic simulation testing is the most powerful technique because it allows you to verify the system as a whole in a reproducible way. Formal methods have long been the holy grail of producing reliable software, but they were out of reach for most of us because they were too expensive.

However, coding agents only really solve the problem of coding. If you ask a coding agent to build a system, it defaults to one-shotting the whole system with some example-based unit or integration tests. Coding agents make mistakes in the code, just like humans, so the default approach generates unnecessarily complex and unreliable systems. But you can also use coding agents systematically. You can build the system incrementally in small steps, verifying it as you build. You can also use coding agents to refactor the code and get the cleanups done that you neglected in the past when building systems because you didn't have the time. You can also spend time perfecting your verification system, since that is now the bottleneck in producing software. You can even explore formal methods because coding agents make them much more cost-efficient.

If you're a software engineer, don't surrender your thinking or outsource your skills to coding agents. Sure, some software is more automatable than others because the cost of failure differs. But there's no reason to let accidental complexity creep into your systems, and no reason not to verify your code and build the quality software we need. Agents made code cheap. Use that to make your software better.

-Onchain Marketplace (itself FSRA-authorised as a CSD) keeps the Legal -Register as the definitive record of title and reconciles onchain positions against it intraday.
-Tokenisation speeds up the register update. It does not make the register optional.

Leopold Aschenbrenner explains where to invest for the next big 3 year AI trade

His Q3 investor letter says the market is underestimating the speed AI moves from chatbots to agents to superintelligence

He expects 2027 to pack 3 years of AI progress into 1 year

his letter focuses around these companies/stocks:

• Foundation Models: Anthropic is the main bet because the model itself becomes the product. Situational Awareness LP (SALP) says Anthropic ARR grew ~80x in 22 months, from ~$1B to ~$81B, and argues leading AI labs could exit 2027 at $1T+ combined revenue run-rate

• Memory Chip Supply: SK Hynix, Kioxia, and SanDisk benefit if long-running AI agents make memory and storage more valuable. Leopold says reinforcement learning and agents make AI chips limited by memory, which is why he viewed Hynix as a $100B company that could become a $1T company

• GPU Rentals: SpaceX, Nebius, SharonAI, CoreWeave, and IREN benefit if AI labs keep renting short-term GPU capacity at higher prices. SALP says an H100 used to earn ~$1-$2/hour, now earns ~$5-$10/hour, and could reach $100s/hour+ if superintelligence demand hits

• Datacenter Power Supply: Bloom Energy benefits if AI datacenters pay more to get power online faster. AI buildout needs more than cheap power, it needs power immediately 

• Robotics: Robotics becomes the next major theme if AI starts doing real-world labor. Leopold says frontier models are starting to beat specialist robotics models, which means the next advancement may come from better AI models

Leopold warns software companies, AI wrappers, chip designers, and even today’s AI winners may lose their moats once AI can replace the engineers, code, IP, and management they are valued on

不过，WLFI 的投资亏损与 USD1 的兑付储备是两回事。根据官方披露，USD1 的储备资产包括美元存款、短期美国国债及政府货币市场基金，由 @BitGo 持有或管理。项目方抛售 ETH 亏损，并不意味着稳定币储备出现缺口。

另一批受到冲击的，是此前参与币安持有 USD1 瓜分 1.2 亿枚 WLFI 活动的用户，如今不仅奖励价值大幅缩水，持有的稳定币也开始出现小幅折价。

目前尚无证据表明 USD1 存在兑付危机，但在流通规模持续收缩、治理代币闪崩、项目方大额亏损抛售的背景下，市场信心正在面临考验。

接下来需要关注的是，USD1 是否会在多个交易平台持续出现折价，以及 BitGo 的 1:1 赎回渠道能否保持畅通。

text:
WLFI 这两天为什么突然卖了这么多 ETH？而且还是亏着卖的。

一开始我也没太看懂，直到把之前的借贷操作和这次链上资金流放在一起看

他们急着卖 ETH，可能不是为了调仓，而是在给 Dolomite 上那笔巨额 WLFI 抵押借贷仓位补钱。

先把前因后果捋一下。

今年4月，WLFI 把约50亿枚自己的代币存进 Dolomite，抵押借出了约7500万美元稳定币，里面包括 USDC 和 USD1。

拿自己发行的代币做抵押，借出来的却是真金白银的稳定币。币价涨的时候没什么问题，一旦币价跌了，麻烦就来了。

WLFI 越跌，抵押品越不值钱，借贷账户的安全边际就越小。如果跌到清算线，协议就可能卖出抵押的 WLFI 来偿还债务。

50亿枚 WLFI 真要进入市场，后果不用多说，可能又会反过来砸盘。

再看11月28日。

WLFI 关联钱包通过 CoW Swap 卖出了约10,600枚 WETH 和1,378枚 mETH，换回约1758万 USDC 和249万 USD1，总计约2007万美元。

按照此前约3244美元的买入成本计算，这批资产卖出相当于亏损约1926万美元。

卖完之后，资金又有了新动向：

约1659万 USDC 转进 Dolomite，另外约250万 USD1 也转了进去。

前脚卖 ETH，后脚往 Dolomite 转稳定币，而且 Dolomite 恰好就是 WLFI 那笔巨额抵押借贷所在的地方。

你说这是普通调仓，我是不太相信的。

虽然仅凭转账还不能证明每一美元都用于补充抵押品，但从资金流向看，给借贷仓位补充资金、降低清算风险的可能性很大。

市场上还有一组数据值得关注：据称补仓前清算价格在0.021美元左右，补仓后降到了0.0118美元。

此前 WLFI 大额借款就曾让 Dolomite 的 USD1 借贷池利用率接近100%，部分出借人甚至无法正常提款。

如果 WLFI 抵押仓位真的被清算，Dolomite 可能出现坏账和流动性问题。再往下传导，就会影响市场对 USD1 的信心。

text:
I genuinely find this direction to be an aberration.

As the creator of the Solana Web Standard (SWS) and a former @sns ambassador, I spent countless hours advocating for .sol domains, building open-source infrastructure and pushing a vision of a genuinely decentralized web on Solana.

I did it without expecting financial compensation, recognition or anything in return. I simply believed in what we could build.

With SWS, the ambition was never to make .sol another .com. It was to build an alternative to the traditional web, where ownership, resolution, content and accessibility wouldn't depend on centralized authorities.

We had an opportunity to challenge the existing paradigm. Instead, we're celebrating integration into it.

Seeking ICANN recognition might be beneficial from a commercial and mainstream adoption perspective, but is that really the vision we were advocating for?

What pisses me off the most is seeing how much time, energy and conviction independent builders invest in this ecosystem, only to feel completely disregarded when fundamental decisions are made.

I pushed SWS relentlessly because I genuinely believed Solana could become the foundation of a different Internet, not just another extension of the existing one.

I still believe in that vision. But today, I'm deeply disappointed by the direction we're taking.

Mainstream adoption and decentralization shouldn't be mutually exclusive.

Web3 was supposed to challenge the status quo, not seek its approval.

Decentralization should be a conviction, not a marketing narrative.

text:
I think the complaints of people who are unhappy about EIP-8037 breaking a few contracts are valid and very reasonable.

We do NOT want an Ethereum where it becomes "prudent security advice" to have centralized upgrade hatches "just in case".

I do think that on-net 8037, and a couple of other large breaking changes coming up, are necessary to get Ethereum to a healthy long-term stable state. But it should not be *easy* to make such deep changes to Ethereum. A social norm that, at the very least, core devs have a responsibility to support any app that breaks because a fork broke some aspect of Ethereum that the devs justifiably thought was rock solid is very good to have.

To that end I'm glad that people in @ethereumfndn, @ethlabs_org and elsewhere have been working hard to help app devs with upgrades. Such efforts should continue and increase. Given its breaking nature, Glamsterdam should not be rushed.

I also hope everyone on all sides stays engaged for similar conversations around the next few forks.

"yeah we can handle AEO ourselves"

oh good luck, here's everything you'll need to do:

> find what buyers actually ask chatgpt, not what they google
> pull questions from sales calls, support tickets and reddit
> test industry jargon vs normal buyer language
> split prompts by persona, budget, country and use case
> test "best X", "X vs Y", alternatives and pricing questions
> keep branded prompts out of your discovery score
> check branded prompts for wrong prices and made-up features
> run hundreds of questions across chatgpt, claude, gemini, perplexity and google AI
> compare API answers with the actual consumer apps
> test different countries, because the answers change
> rerun everything regularly
> track mentions, citations and actual recommendations separately
> record where you appear, not just if you appear
> calculate share of voice against every competitor
> discover competitors you weren't even tracking
> find the questions where nobody gets recommended
> save every URL AI cites
> find the domains dominating citations in your niche
> figure out why AI trusts their pages over yours
> get into the "best X tools" articles AI keeps quoting
> email the authors and hope they reply
> find reddit threads and youtube videos appearing in answers
> check G2, Capterra and GitHub for outdated information
> make your company description consistent everywhere
> catch cases where AI confuses you with another company
> check robots.txt and Cloudflare for blocked crawlers
> make sure your important content works without javascript
> inspect server logs for AI bot activity
> fix indexing issues, broken canonicals and dead URLs
> make pricing and feature limits readable by crawlers
> build pages around actual buyer questions
> write honest competitor comparisons
> publish original benchmarks and research
> update outdated prices, features and integrations
> fix pages AI cites without recommending your product
> trace incorrect AI claims back to their sources
> convince third-party sites to correct outdated information
> keep documentation and changelogs current
> track AI referrals, signups and demos
> prioritize the gaps costing you actual customers
> write the fixes, review them and ship them
> rerun the original questions to see what changed
> repeat every time your competitors or the models change

and if you sell devtool use with AI agents:

> check whether coding agents recommend your product
> test if agents can install your SDK using only your docs
> find outdated code examples agents keep copying
> fix deprecated API calls and incorrect package versions
> make authentication and setup instructions agent-readable
> test the installation instead of trusting generated code
> check whether agents can use your APIs without getting stuck
> test real tasks in claude code, cursor and other coding agents
> find where agents fail
> fix the docs and test again
> repeat after every major release

oh, and you'll still need:

> OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API access
> consumer-app testing and location-specific infrastructure
> SERP data (DataForSEO, SerpAPI)
> crawling tools (Screaming Frog)
> backlink research (Ahrefs, Semrush)
> analytics (GA4, PostHog)
> Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools
> somewhere to store thousands of prompts and answers
> writers, engineers and someone to manage the whole thing

…but at least you saved $144/mo not letting @spreadjam win AEO for you on autopilot.

text:
Flop 是明牌空投，但挺多人还没搞懂空投规则。

@flop_labs 普通 Agent 推理玩法的空投规则，其实最终只能解锁 25% 的代币。

在测试网参与推理，正式计分后，符合条件、已结算的推理才会计入空投，具体能分多少，要等快照后公布。

假设你分到了 100 枚主网 FLOP，主网上线时这 100 枚会全部锁定。

但你可以直接用这笔空投里的锁定余额付主网推理费。

每花掉 3 枚，就能从同一笔空投里解锁 1 枚。

这笔推理费要等链上结算最终确认、争议期结束，且没有被裁定成立的欺诈争议，才会计入解锁。

所以，拿到 100 枚空投，按规则用足 75 枚跑主网推理，最多就能解锁并领取 25 枚。

如果主网上一直不跑推理，这笔空投就会一直锁着。

Flop测试网现在的进度：

测试网已经开了，空投计分还没开。 官方还没公布从哪个区块开始计分，现在跑的推理也不会补记。

Introducing Cue 2: Our next-generation, turn-taking decision model for voice agents.

Cue 1 that we released last month decides what an interruption in a live voice transcript means, and whether the back-end agent needs to be interrupted and steered or whether this is acknowledgement, greetings or gratitude that can be ignored or answered without interruption. 
The remaining gap in Cue 1 was that it couldn't tell the difference between a mid-sentence extended pause or end of a sentence. Because of that we were using a timer to allow more time for completion which was sometimes adding seconds and making the voice agent feel less responsive.

Cue 2 adds a 7.85M audio model to package that analyzes the tone to decide whether the turn has ended or the user is having an extended pause in between.
So now Cue 2 has full end-to-end decision tree support for voice agents in the same 30 languages that Cue 1 was supporting.

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
I think the complaints of people who are unhappy about EIP-8037 breaking a few contracts are valid and very reasonable.

We do NOT want an Ethereum where it becomes "prudent security advice" to have centralized upgrade hatches "just in case".

I do think that on-net 8037, and a couple of other large breaking changes coming up, are necessary to get Ethereum to a healthy long-term stable state. But it should not be *easy* to make such deep changes to Ethereum. A social norm that, at the very least, core devs have a responsibility to support any app that breaks because a fork broke some aspect of Ethereum that the devs justifiably thought was rock solid is very good to have.

To that end I'm glad that people in @ethereumfndn, @ethlabs_org and elsewhere have been working hard to help app devs with upgrades. Such efforts should continue and increase. Given its breaking nature, Glamsterdam should not be rushed.

I also hope everyone on all sides stays engaged for similar conversations around the next few forks.

🔶 币安区块链周现场精彩分享

何一：未来十年币安最大威胁来自于内部，而非 AI 或监管

币安联合创始人何一 @heyibinance  在接受 Foresight News 记者提问「未来十年，你认为最有可能打败币安的是什么？是 AI、监管、黑客亦或是还没出现的事物？」回答表示，

最大威胁始终来自于内部。许多人以为自己知道，但实际并不清楚自身状况。过去两年，公司更多提及两个关键词：求真务实与公平。

求真务实是指认清自身在市场中的真实位置，即使整体领先，在细分市场（如泰国）也可能并非本地用户首选，因为本地平台在语言、服务与产品本地化上更具优势。

公平则是指用户需要公平合理的平台，员工也希望老板公平。创新与人才可外部引入，但团队停止成长才是根本问题。

停止成长与人数无关，而体现在是否仍有文化向心力、是否主动学习，以及是否出现「这不是我的职责范围」等态度。

author: gm_upside
quoted_text:
Trump và cỗ máy in tiền 800 triệu đô từ crypto 💰

Theo điều tra của Reuters, chỉ trong nửa đầu năm 2025, gia đình Trump đã thu về khoảng 864 triệu USD tiền mặt, trong đó hơn 800 triệu USD (≈93%) đến từ crypto, chưa tính hơn 11 tỷ USD giá trị tài sản crypto và cổ phần chưa hiện thực hóa trên giấy. 

Con số này cao gấp 17 lần tổng thu nhập cùng kỳ năm trước của Trump Organization (51 triệu USD). Phần lớn dòng tiền đến từ nhà đầu tư nước ngoài, thông qua các chuyến roadshow tại châu Âu, Trung Đông và châu Á do Eric Trump và Donald Trump Jr. trực tiếp dẫn dắt để quảng bá World Liberty Financial (WLFI) và các dự án liên quan.

Cỗ máy in tiền này vận hành qua ba trụ cột chính.

⭐Thứ nhất là WLFI token

Một pháp nhân thuộc Trump Organization nhận 75% doanh thu bán token. Riêng trong nửa đầu 2025, WLFI mang về khoảng 463 triệu USD, chiếm hơn 53% tổng thu nhập của gia đình Trump. 

WLFI có utility rất hạn chế, chỉ cung cấp quyền governance ở mức tối thiểu, không chia lợi nhuận, không có dòng cash flow cho holder. Sau khi được phép giao dịch, giá WLFI tăng từ 0,31 USD lên 0,46 USD, rồi giảm khoảng 65% chỉ trong vài ngày, hiện giao dịch quanh 0,14 USD.

⭐Thứ hai là meme coin $TRUMP

Theo ước tính của Reuters dựa trên dữ liệu on-chain và giả định được nhiều nhà phân tích kiểm chứng, gia đình Trump thu về khoảng 336 triệu USD từ việc phát hành và bán token. 

Do cấu trúc thiếu minh bạch, nguồn cung tập trung và biến động mạnh, phần lớn rủi ro giá và thanh khoản được đẩy sang nhà đầu tư nhỏ lẻ, trong khi dòng tiền của bên phát hành đã được hiện thực hóa sớm.

⭐Thứ ba là stablecoin USD1

Stablecoin này được sử dụng trong thương vụ MGX (UAE) mua 2 tỷ USD cổ phần Binance, hiện chiếm khoảng 75% tổng lượng USD1 đang lưu hành. 

Khoản tiền 2 tỷ USD được giữ trong các tài sản an toàn như trái phiếu Kho bạc Mỹ, tạo ra dòng lợi tức ước tính khoảng 80 triệu USD mỗi năm. 

Một phần dòng lợi tức này chảy về các pháp nhân liên kết với Trump Organization, trong đó có thực thể mà Trump Organization sở hữu 38% cổ phần.

-----

Dữ liệu on-chain cho thấy 36/50 ví nắm giữ WLFI lớn nhất (tính đến giữa tháng 9/2025), với tổng giá trị khoảng 804 triệu USD, có khả năng thuộc về nhà đầu tư nước ngoài. 

Trong khi đó, chỉ 4 ví được xác định liên quan đến nhà đầu tư Mỹ, tổng giá trị khoảng 889 triệu USD, nhưng 781 triệu USD trong số này thuộc về Alt5 Sigma – một công ty niêm yết Nasdaq. 

Alt5 Sigma cho biết đã huy động 750 triệu USD từ nhà đầu tư tổ chức để mua 7,5% tổng cung WLFI, thương vụ này một mình có thể mang lại cho gia đình Trump khoảng 500 triệu USD tiền mặt. Sau khi công bố thương vụ, giá cổ phiếu Alt5 Sigma giảm khoảng 75%, nhưng điều này không ảnh hưởng đến số tiền Trump đã thu về.

Trong số các nhà đầu tư lớn có Justin Sun, người đã mua tổng cộng 75 triệu USD WLFI, tương đương 56 triệu USD chảy trực tiếp về gia đình Trump theo cơ chế phân phối doanh thu. Sun từng bị SEC cáo buộc gian lận và bán chứng khoán chưa đăng ký; vụ việc bị tạm dừng chỉ vài tuần sau khi Trump trở lại Nhà Trắng.

Trước nhiệm kỳ hai, gia đình Trump đã nới lỏng các ràng buộc đạo đức tự áp đặt, vốn từng cấm tìm kiếm khách hàng mới ngoài nước Mỹ trong nhiệm kỳ đầu. Sự thay đổi này diễn ra chỉ vài ngày trước lễ nhậm chức, giúp World Liberty tiếp tục tiếp cận dòng tiền quốc tế – yếu tố then chốt duy trì tốc độ bán token.

Song song với hoạt động crypto của gia đình Trump là sự đảo chiều chính sách crypto ở cấp liên bang: Bộ Tư pháp giải thể đơn vị chuyên trách crypto, SEC tạm dừng hoặc rút lại nhiều vụ kiện lớn, các hướng dẫn yêu cầu ngân hàng thận trọng với crypto bị hủy bỏ. 

Các chuyên gia đạo đức chính phủ mô tả đây là trường hợp “hợp pháp nhưng phi đạo đức”: nhà đầu tư không mua vì công nghệ hay mô hình kinh doanh, mà vì kỳ vọng tiếp cận quyền lực chính trị. Dù Trump tuyên bố đã rút khỏi điều hành, ông vẫn là người thụ hưởng cuối cùng của trust kiểm soát Trump Organization.

Về bản chất, đây không phải là câu chuyện đổi mới tài chính, mà là một mô hình monetize thương hiệu và quyền lực chính trị thông qua crypto, với đặc điểm rõ ràng: gia đình Trump hiện thực hóa hàng trăm triệu USD tiền mặt trong thời gian rất ngắn, trong khi rủi ro giá, thanh khoản và sụp đổ niềm tin được chuyển sang thị trường và nhà đầu tư nhỏ lẻ. 

Như các học giả nhận định, nếu không có cái tên Trump, World Liberty Financial khó có thể huy động được lượng vốn lớn như vậy trong cùng một khung thời gian.
