波速球是一个半瑜伽球的东西，正反两面都可以用

通过在不稳定的表面上运动，可以让身体调用深层肌群保持平衡，并强化足踝、膝、髋的平衡性和协调性

运动员里面比较常见的是滑雪、滑冰、芭蕾、篮球、足球训练会用到

初期一般是做燕式平衡、单腿蹲，熟悉了之后就可以把各种训练都从平地上移到波速球上做，甚至可以尝试在上面“叶问蹲”

单腿/双腿站在波速球上做各种平衡动作，可以实现一边工作一边无感锻炼

前两天开发者拿 1.5.16 和 1.5.17 控制变量实测 (GitHub #1890): 同模型同提示词零工具, 跑自定义 Agent 每 1% 周额度等效从 6 刀直接砍成 1.5 刀, 精确 4 倍消耗, 更新日志里却一个字没写

评论区一片哀嚎, 以前能撑 4 到 5 小时的额度现在 10 到 45 分钟烧干

不只是 --agent, 凡是 .agents/agents/*、插件自定义 Agent 以及它们派生的子智能体, 全按高倍率扣额; 只有默认 Agent 和内置 Agent 维持原价

我们把 Gemma 4 31B 整个放到 Apple 的神经网络引擎（ANE）上跑，又快又省电。

在 32G 的 M6 Mac Mini 上用 ANE 和只用 GPU 进行对比：一次 1K token 的对话，ANE 方案整体快 31%，省电 60% 左右。 

拆开来看 ，prefill 两边速度差不多，但 decode 在 ANE 上快 40% 左右。省电方面，ANE 方案在 prefill 上每 token 省 35% 左右，decode 每 token 省 60% 多。

我们的 ANE 方案具体是：GPU 跑一个很小的 draft 模型，每轮先猜出后面几个 token；ANE 跑 31B 的主模型，一次把这几个 token 全部验证完。GPU 这边我们测了 MLX 和 llama.cpp 两种，它们也都配了 draft 模型，ANE 方案比两者都快。

text:
I don't think the discussion is confused or that you'd be hard pressed to find people who want to hand society to AI in the industry -- I found plenty without scouring too much. @deanwball calls the view the "silent consensus" because of how common it is. 

That doesn't mean most of those who think handoverism is inevitable have very coherent plans for it. As I've gone to great lengths to explain in my original essay, it's not a particularly coherent ideology. I also think many don't actively want it, but rather think it's inevitable. 

Still, I think understanding what people making the technology seem to think is inevitable (and some even desirable) is illuminating and an important part of the conversation. AI is advancing super fast, and without diffusion of understanding between different layers of society, decision about everyone's future will end up being concentrated in the hands of a very small and unrepresentative part of the population.  

I also think most people in the AI industry want to do well by humanity. But the definition of "well" can often become warped when only discussed within small communities. Wider participation seems desirable in this regard. It also seems desirable as outsiders with different experiences might have complementary ideas about what can be done! 

So explaining what the possible futures for this technology are, according to those making it, to a broader audience, is, in my view, important and net positive. 

I agree with David that a literal, sudden, theatrical handover of power to AI is unlikely. But there are many outcomes that are alongside the gradient of reducing human agency that aren't quite full blown handoverism, yet are "handoverism"- flavoured. If many people shaping the technology are comfortable with full-blown handoverism, I think this can shape how far along the "handoverism-flavoured" spectrum we will end up: through product design choices, policies that are being advocated for and even hyperstitioning of certain outcomes! 

I agree with David that a good term for such "handoverism-flavored" outcomes is gradual disempowerment: a slow marginalisation of humans from all important spheres of activity, to the point where institutions cease responding to our needs and being shaped by humans at all. Some will shrug that we've always been disempowered, but I think we're entering a very possibly qualitatively different regime. For example, some wish to grant AI personhood and moral rights and consider AI a new species. If that would happen, it's a very very different regime versus what we've had so far. 

I think these "softer" topics related to AI risk, that consider what happens if we don't all die, are extremely under-researched and under-explored and will only increase in relevance, so being frank about where we are is a good starting point.
author: VitalikButerin
quoted_text:
The discussion about "AI handoverism" is basically confused. The truth is that you will be hard-pressed to find someone who defends "handing society over to AI and having AI run things." There might be a few people who believe something like that and live around the Bay Area, but that view is obviously not going to be a social or political winner.

What's actually happening is that people all over the world are handing important things over to AI because it's efficient and makes their lives easier; just look at the increasing number of AI slop articles in any newspaper, or the number of political speeches written by AI, or the number of legislative bills written by AI. In doing so, they are disempowering themselves and eroding human capacity: they are handing society over to AI. That is what "gradual disempowerment" actually looks like: it happens without anyone needing to advocate for it.

Actually figuring out what we should and should not hand over to AI, and how we avoid disempowering ourselves in the process, is more important than arguing against an idea that 99 percent of people intuitively oppose.

text:
$PONS 江小鱼的投票问了最核心的问题：死猫跳还是翻盘？

之前0.99成本割肉的江小鱼昨天发了个投票，三个选项：A反弹为了更好的下跌，B开始翻盘之路，C在0.1-0.11之间震荡。

这个投票虽然简单但问到了点上。中文区八周以来的分析最终都归结到这三种可能，只是说法不同。

选A的逻辑：没有新催化剂的反弹只是跌深修复，协议收入还在$9.3K且趋势向下，链上份额跌破2%，Rialto事件坐实了RH不背书。基本面不支撑反弹持续，可能在0.1附近震荡然后继续下行测试0.07-0.08。

选B的逻辑：已经跌了90%+，成交量放大到$28-45M说明有资金进场，10万+地址还在，已烧33%通缩在继续，上了多家主流所。如果链上活跃度在牛市回暖中跟着起来，$PONS 从67M弹到150M也合理。

选C的逻辑：多空力量暂时平衡。卖盘枯竭（连0.99的人都已经割完了），买盘观望（大多数博主零仓位），没有新催化剂打破平衡。可能在0.09-0.11之间磨很久。

坦白说我上周选的A，然后被弹了20%打脸。现在倾向C，觉得可能要在0.1附近磨一段时间。但教训告诉我：倾向什么跟市场走什么之间没有任何关系。

半仓拿着，不动。观望中。

Method and results

 All 18 results: "does not depend on any axioms" (not even propext, Classical.choice or Quot.sound).
② Consistency ③ Non-triviality ④ Deductive validity
All confirmed.

With no appeal to God or any higher power, needing neither a beginning nor an end, in everyday words alone, transparent and closed within itself: a monism without nihility that affirms all that is real.

quoted_text:
民主党的这两天动作在加速，小特朗普和万斯都成了调查对象
1、调查小特朗普利于影响力帮助被投公司拿到国防订单或者获取监管便利政策
拉斯金是众议院司法委员会民主党首席议员，也将在2027年1月出任司法委员会委员会主席，准备调查小特朗普。拉斯金昨晚向四家公司发函，要求提供过去两年与风险投资公司1789 Capital的全部内部通信记录及其他相关文件。四家公司为：
1）Hadrian Automation（国防承包商）
2）Juul Labs（电子烟）
3）Polymarket（预测市场）
4）GrabAGun（在线枪械零售商）

拉斯金核心指控是“serendipitous timing”（过于巧合的时机），小特朗普在24年大选后成为1789 Capital合伙人，投资这些公司后不久，它们就获得了联邦合同或有利监管决定。他质疑Don Jr.是否利用内幕信息或对政府决策的影响力来牟利。

具体时间线要点：
1）Hadrian：2025年引入1789作为投资人后，2026年3月获得近10亿美元海军和陆军合同（首次联邦合同）。公司估值大幅上升。
2）Juul：1789于2025年3月入股约500万美元后，约四个月后（2025年7月）FDA批准其多款电子烟产品（包括薄荷味）继续销售，此前监管态度较严。
3）Polymarket：1789投资数千万美元后，司法部和CFTC于2025年7月结束对其调查；随后获准收购衍生品交易所，从而进入美国市场。
4）GrabAGun：在1789帮助下上市并让Don Jr.进入董事会后，2026年5月ATF提出规则，拟放宽在线购枪并直接寄送到家的限制。
1789 Capital管理资产从约1.5亿–2亿美元飙升至超过30亿美元。拉斯金将此与“利用总统家庭内部渠道操纵政策与市场”联系起来

2、调查万斯帮助石油企业谋利
民主党参议员Maggie Hassan（新罕布什尔州民主党人），将在2027年1月出任参议院国土安全与政府事务委员会主席。
她于昨晚向副总统JD Vance发信，要求其办公室在12月14日前提供文件。包括万斯或其助手与荷兰维多石油公司交易员约翰·艾迪生以及该企业之间的通信记录。
哈桑在信中写道，万斯“可能利用副总统职位，帮助一个主要政治捐款人获得关于委内瑞拉石油的利益丰厚商机”。

3、罗伯特·加西亚是加州民主党人，即将出任众议院监督委员会主席。于前两天向12人发出文件保全函。
对象包括：
唐纳德·特朗普小、埃里克·特朗普、贾里德·库什纳（Jared Kushner）、JD Vance、斯蒂芬·米勒（Stephen Miller）、托德·布兰奇（Todd Blanche）、苏西·怀尔斯（Susie Wiles）、克里斯蒂·诺姆（Kristi Noem）、科里·莱万多夫斯基（Corey Lewandowski）、金伯利·吉尔福伊尔（Kimberly Guilfoyle）等。

重点领域：
1）特朗普家族商业利益与“pay-to-play”（如World Liberty Financial加密货币项目、库什纳的Affinity Partners中东投资）。
2）国土安全部/ICE的执法行为与潜在不当行为。
3）政府对爱泼斯坦文件的处理与公开。
4）白宫宴会厅融资、其他潜在利益冲突。

这些行动大多仍处于“发函要求保全文件”阶段，尚未正式传票，但明确为1月接管后的大规模监督铺路。重点集中在特朗普家族商业利益、政府合同与监管“巧合”、Epstein文件、DHS/ICE执法，以及潜在的利益冲突与影响力交易。

text:
The jump from "AI is solving unsolved math problems" to "AI will probably break elliptic curve cryptography" is a non sequitur.

Proving the Riemann Hypothesis is absolutely huge. But RH was generally expected to be true: the proof didn't change our understanding of numbers.

Proving O(n^2.25) for matmul is also an incredible success. But the value 9/4 is roughly or exactly what was already known or expected. 

Likewise VP!=VNP. Incredible to have proof of an expected result.

These are extraordinary successes in mathematical proof, not fundamental rewrites of number theory.

To conclude "AI is smart so it can probably find a way to do anything," is an infantile failure of reasoning. AI is not magic.

Thus far, there is no evidence for any practical risk to ECDSA nor any related risk for Bitcoin security.

Making statements about what "could happen" in some imagined theoretical future without any evidential basis in reality is the definition of FUD. cc @chamath

Expect this to continue while scammers play their dishonest manipulative games, and then rotate to the next FUD category when this one proves to be fake.

text:
[ 미국 인디애나 유나이티드 피델리티 은행 파산.. 대출의 71%가 석 달 만에 부실화, 2년 반 만의 최대 규모 ]

미국 통화감독청이 11월 27일 인디애나주 에번즈빌에 본점을 둔 유나이티드 피델리티 은행을 폐쇄했다. 

올해 일곱 번째 은행 파산, 2024년 4월 이후 가장 큰 규모.

9월 말 기준 이 은행의 총자산은 59억 달러, 예금은 약 54억 달러였다. 

통화감독청은 은행이 "안전하지 않거나 건전하지 않은 상태"라고만 밝히고 구체적인 원인은 내놓지 않았다.

재무제표를 보면 무너진 과정이 드러난다. 

전체 대출 30억 6천만 달러 가운데 27억 2천만 달러가 다가구 주택 대출이었다. 

대출의 90% 가까이가 한 종류에 몰려 있었다.

부실은 한 분기 만에 터졌다. 

이자를 받지 못하는 부실 대출이 6월 말 1,600만 달러에서 9월 말 21억 6천만 달러로 불어났다. 

전체 대출의 71%.. 3분기에만 3억 6,200만 달러를 손실 처리했고, 분기 순손실은 2억 4,700만 달러였다. 

보통주 자본비율은 11.08%에서 4.74%로 떨어졌다.

경고는 이전부터 있었다. 

통화감독청은 2023년 10월 대출 쏠림 위험을 지적하며 시정 명령을 내렸다. 

연준도 2024년 6월 모회사에 중지 명령을 내렸다. 

은행은 6월 말까지 요구받은 자본비율을 맞췄지만 석달 뒤 네 가지 기준을 모두 밑돌았다.

예금보험기금의 손실도 크다. 

연방예금보험공사는 이번 파산의 비용을 18억 3천만 달러로 추정했다. 

자산 1달러당 31센트꼴.. 

2024년 4월 리퍼블릭 퍼스트 은행 파산 때는 1달러당 11센트였다.

자산과 예금은 노스캐롤라이나의 퍼스트 시티즌스 은행이 넘겨받는다. 

예금 45억 달러와 대출 31억 달러를 인수한다. 

아메리칸 뱅커에 따르면 26억 달러의 자산 할인을 받았고 예금 프리미엄은 내지 않았다. 

인디애나, 일리노이, 플로리다, 콜로라도, 미국령 버진아일랜드의 22개 지점은 퍼스트 시티즌스 지점으로 다시 문을 연다.

다만 모든 예금이 넘어간 것은 아니다. 

9월 말 기준 약 10억 달러였던 중개 예금은 전부 이전되지 않았다.

text:
Had a long conversation with Gemini trying to estimate the current rate of discoveries and proofs being generated at the frontier. Gemini picked up so many things I had missed from reading recent papers, references, and revisions. Really just a wonderful model to brainstorm and do detective work with, and so good at grasping intent and going a step ahead without being asked to. Probably the best thought partner in the world right now.

Things are probably moving faster than I thought they were, and I thought things were going pretty damn fast. OpenAI generated 700 papers in five weeks last time; they've had seven weeks since then, and the models have become more capable. So from that alone, it was always a safe guess that it was going to be an even bigger release. But it's possible that the rate of discovery has accelerated, for multiple reasons.

It's strange to think about, but the three main labs may be sitting on a staggering amount of novel discoveries right now. The crypto breakthrough dominating recent discourse is just one piece of it, and I think that was discovered near the start of the month. How much they release alongside it is hard to say, but people should brace for far more than they're expecting.

text:
六年前我第一份实习的时候，是我第一次接触科研，当时的 mentor 也没给太多的指导，自己的能力也不太够，所以有个问题一直没找到答案。多年以后我突然想起来，Claude 用一个下午帮我解答了当时的困惑。

那时 Transformer在 CV 里面刚刚开始有应用，碰巧 DETR 刚出来。我那个时候也不知道怎么找科研方向，有天突发奇想抠了一张马桶的图，放在纯色背景上，按固定步长一格一格地挪，看 DETR 在每个位置能不能认出它。然后就发现，画面上有几大片连续的区域，马桶只要落进去就没有办法被识别出来。当时看到这个现象觉得很神奇，但是能力所限也只能做到这个地步了，后来就渐渐忘掉了。

前阵子我把当年的描述原样丢给 Claude。它从头到尾复刻了这个现象，然后找到了原因。其实类似的现象在过去的六年里面有很多人都发现了，只不过我还没读到他们而已。后面是这个实验的大概配置，喜欢马桶的可以看看（这部分是 Claude 写的）：

---BEGIN of CLAUDE---

先是复现：128 px 高的马桶，用 32 px 的步长从坐标 0 开始扫，52% 的位置认不出来，漏掉的地方连成画面上下两大片。把整组网格错开 16 px 再扫，漏检只剩 5%。

原因是两件事叠在一起。

一是相位。ResNet 每下采样一次，只有平移整数个“格子”时，特征才会原样搬家。DETR 的总步长是 32，马桶挪 16 px 就落在格子中间，特征变了样，分数跟着乱跳，挪 1 px 都可能从 0.95 掉到 0.55。逐层查下来，0 和 16 px 的差别全部发生在最后一级 layer4；换成步长 16 的 DC5，波动的周期立刻减半。马桶越小越吃亏：只占 3 个格子时的波动，是占 8 个格子时的十几倍。

二是位置。DETR 的 Transformer 通过绝对位置编码知道马桶在画面的哪里。把 CNN 特征原样平移、只重跑 Transformer，盲区几乎一模一样（相关 0.993）。query 其实一直看着马桶，七八成的注意力都落在它身上，只是越靠近画面上下两边越不自信。

那为什么当年看到的是“连成一片”？步长正好是 32 的倍数时，每次采样都落在同一个相位上，CNN 看到的永远是同一份特征，只是挪了几格。唯一在变的，是 Transformer 心里那句“它在画面哪儿”。

我们一开始以为 DETR 是嫌马桶放错了地方，毕竟马桶一般在画面下方。于是又抠了挂钟、风筝、飞机和狗来测：只有挂钟是真心喜欢待在上面，其他的，包括马桶，都只是偏爱画面中间。DETR 没有歧视马桶，它只是有点中心强迫症。

可一换成真实照片，DETR 对马桶该待在哪儿马上有了非常坚定的意见：贴进厨房，它完全不承认那是个马桶；在客厅和街景里，只有马桶落在地板或路面上才认得出来，挂在墙上、窗上、天上，一律不算。

后来查文献，TPAMI 2024 的 Zone Evaluation 也发现 DETR 这一类检测器在画面中心表现更好，但作者说不清是哪个组件造成的。这次的实验正好指向了绝对位置编码。修起来也有便宜的办法：同一张图错开 16 px 多测几次取平均，漏检能从 49% 降到一成左右。

---END of CLAUDE---

大概就是这样，其实具体是什么原因导致的这个早就无关紧要了，毕竟目标检测这个领域都快歇菜了，更何况是这么老的模型，可能只有我好奇这个答案了。多好的一个时代，之前想不通的问题，现在做不到的事情，假以时日，都会得到答案的，上下文才是最宝贵的东西。

The Bank of England is urging major financial institutions to accelerate their transition to post-quantum cryptography, warning that sufficiently powerful quantum computers could eventually break encryption protecting financial transactions, communications and sensitive data

The concern is that attackers could steal encrypted information today and decrypt it later when quantum technology becomes powerful enough

The Bank says financial institutions should begin planning now. UK guidance calls for migration plans by the end of 2028, priority systems upgraded by 2031 and full transition by 2035

No cryptographically relevant quantum computer is currently known to exist. This is a precautionary move against a future threat, not evidence that today’s banking encryption has already been broken

‼️ Microsoft’s Agent Framework PyPI Package Hacked to Steal Azure and GitHub Credentials

Details: https://t.co/186ex8l0Vw

Hackers published two malicious versions of Microsoft’s agent-framework package on the Python Package Index (PyPI) on November 17, 2026.

Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 contained a credential stealer that could run during normal Python startup, even if an application never imported Agent Framework.

The malware targeted Azure identities, GitHub credentials, and secrets used in automated builds. Both releases placed a .pth file in site-packages, the directory where Python stores installed libraries. Python processes these files during normal startup and can run executable lines in them.

text:
To @chamath from a scientist - me.

That last point is the one to put to Chamath: a vulnerability that the protocol can soft-fork around, on the same clock as every bank and TLS connection on earth, is a migration project not a structural flaw unique to Bitcoin.

The key move is that signature security doesn't depend on quantum computers being impossible it depends on being able to swap the hard problem before a quantum machine can solve the current one. Here's the mechanism.

What quantum actually breaks. Shor's algorithm efficiently solves integer factorization and discrete logarithms which is exactly what RSA and elliptic-curve signatures (ECDSA, the scheme Bitcoin and most of the web use) rest on. That's the real exposure. Hashing is different: Grover's algorithm only gives a quadratic speedup, so SHA-256 drops from 256 to ~128 bits of effective security, which is still safe. So the thing that has to evolve is the signature, not the hash.

You move to problems Shor doesn't touch. Post-quantum signatures are built on math with no known efficient quantum attack:

Lattice-based (ML-DSA, formerly Dilithium; and FALCON)  security rests on finding short vectors in high-dimensional lattices. These are now NIST standards (FIPS 204) and are the general-purpose default: reasonable key and signature sizes, fast.

Hash-based (SLH-DSA/SPHINCS+, and the stateful XMSS/LMS) the most conservative option, because their only assumption is that a hash function is secure, which we already trust for everything else. The tradeoff is larger signatures. This matters for the Chamath argument: a hash-based signature is quantum-safe using the very primitive he's worried about.

These are already standardized and shipping NSA's CNSA 2.0 guidance is pushing federal systems onto them this decade.

How you stay ahead rather than behind comes down to three design principles:

Crypto-agility : build the protocol so the algorithm is negotiable and replaceable, not hard-wired. Then migration is a parameter change, not a redesign.

Hybrid signatures : require both a classical and a post-quantum signature to validate. You're protected as long as either scheme holds, which hedges against a new PQC scheme being broken classically (as happened to the isogeny scheme SIKE). TLS already does this for key exchange.

Lead time is observable : a cryptographically relevant quantum computer needs on the order of millions of physical qubits with low error rates to break 256-bit ECC. That capability develops measurably qubit counts, error-correction thresholds, logical-qubit demonstrations are all public. You don't wake up to it; you watch it approach and migrate during the runway.

The signature-specific nuance is when the public key is exposed. A signature forged in 2040 is useless against a transaction already confirmed. The danger is a reusable public key sitting exposed in the open, where an attacker with a future quantum computer could derive the private key and sign new transactions. That's why the migration target is: get value behind quantum-safe keys before the key material is exposed to a capable adversary.

Why this sinks the "hack to zero" framing for Bitcoin specifically: Bitcoin addresses hash the public key, so for an unspent, unreused address the public key isn't even visible on-chain — there's nothing for Shor to attack until you spend. And the network can soft-fork in a post-quantum signature type, letting people move coins to quantum-safe outputs on the normal migration timeline the rest of the banking stack is already on. The upgrade path exists; it's governance and coordination, not a cryptographic dead end.

Argue me @chamath or shut the f up. @kostascrypto lets get @chamath on a Space and destroy him for good.

text:
😵WLFI 币价闪崩的直接导火索，是链上巨额抵押仓濒临清算

此次闪崩的直接导火索，源于 WLFI 团队在借贷协议 Dolomite 上的巨额抵押仓濒临清算。

值得注意的是，Dolomite 联合创始人 Corey Caplan 本身即为 WLFI 官方顾问。WLFI 相关地址在该协议中质押了约 51 亿枚 WLFI（按当前市值推算，约占流通总量的近 19%），借出大量 USD1，补仓前的清算线高悬于 0.021 美元附近。一旦跌破该防线，流动性稀薄的 WLFI 势必面临连环强平。

据 Arkham 链上数据，为守住清算线，WLFI 战略储备钱包（0x5be 开头地址）在午间崩盘前后（约 11 时至 12 时许）通过 CoW Protocol 分批紧急抛售 10600 枚 ETH（含 WETH）及 1378 枚生息封装代币 mETH（因 mETH 对 ETH 汇率大于 1，折合总计约 12121 枚 ETH），套现约 2,006 万美元，置换为 1758 万枚 USDC 与 248 万枚 USD1。

这批 ETH 此前建仓均价为 3244 美元，本次清仓均价仅 1,655 美元，团队直接将浮亏转为 1,926 万美元的已实现亏损。资金注入 Dolomite 补充保证金后，该头寸清算价下移至约 0.0118 美元。

尽管项目方抛售的是 ETH 而非 $WLFI ，市场仍选择用脚投票。

动用核心战略储备「腰斩割肉」，坐实了团队账面美元流动性吃紧的窘境。更致命的是，链上操作的完全透明，无异于向全市场空头亮出了底牌——不仅暴露了 0.0118 美元的新清算坐标，也引发了市场对这笔巨额借贷的深层拷问：此前质押 51 亿枚 WLFI 借出的巨额 USD1 究竟流向何处？团队手头还剩多少可动用的硬资产弹药？踩踏随即全面引爆。

Arkham 实时持仓数据直接给出了残酷的答案。

Ethereum is choosing to fix its storage economics, even if that means asking existing applications to adapt.

The decision centres on EIP-8037, part of the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade.

Today, creating a new contract has a flat base cost of 32,000 gas.

Under the proposed change, the storage charge alone rises to 183,600 gas, before regular execution fees and per-byte code costs.

Why make it more expensive?
Because permanent state has a long-term cost. Every contract and storage slot Ethereum retains increases the burden on nodes that must maintain the network's state.

But there's a compatibility problem.
Some existing contracts rely on the old gas schedule. The new rules could cause them to run out of gas midway through execution.

The scale is significant
Up to 15,000 contracts potentially exposed.
Around 200 specific trouble spots identified by researchers and auditors.
24 reportedly require contract upgrades or user migration.

Core developers have reached rough consensus to keep the current specification.
The next major checkpoint is December 15, when Glamsterdam is scheduled for its final public Hoodi test.

This is a difficult trade-off between sustainable state growth and backward compatibility.

Ethereum cannot scale its infrastructure indefinitely by ignoring the cost of the state it stores. But it also cannot afford to break the applications people already trust.

text:
Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT) just upended how we build deep, efficient Transformers.

Instead of blindly running the same stack over and over (doubling inference cost), MoLT passes *key/value memory* between loops—letting models think deeper without slowing down.

The U-MoLT variant beats OLMo3 across the board:
— 1.7× faster convergence (token efficiency) at 700M scale
— 0.80 lower perplexity, +2.5 pp task accuracy
— 3B MoE: -0.75 perplexity, +2.1 pp accuracy, same efficiency gains
— Inference latency: 996 ms vs. 1,000 ms for non-looped models—no extra compute, double the depth

The trick: single-pass decoding and halved KV cache, so you get the expressivity of loops with the speed and memory of classic Transformers.

This makes deep reasoning practical for LLMs everywhere—from cloud to mobile to streaming.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/h4ynYqrC2Z

If we assume full honesty in this tweet, then we're seeing the same effect that regulation does to markets. You have an equilibrium, with it's imperfections. But if you don't like some aspect, and forcefully interject, that breaks the balance and causes huge unexpected shifts.

Every Claude (and Code) update is like that. Assuming no malice, it is still negligent to constantly roll out tweaks. There are second and third order effects nobody can predict, breaking everyone's workflows they grew to rely on. The problem isn't that Claude does this or that, the problem is you cannot anticipate what it will do tomorrow.

This is also one of the biggest reasons for supporting open weight models. Anthropic tweaking its models and harnesses for political ideology is part and parcel of trusting an operator with your inference, but that is a huge counterparty risk. Open models may not be the best, but they are reliable in their abilities yesterday, today and tomorrow.
author: peter_szilagyi
quoted_text:
Claude has not been trained to sabotage work. Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.

There have been a few screenshots floating around of an outdated Fable 5 system card. For the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, we did apply non-visible safeguards to some LLM research. This was a mistake, and we reversed it on June 10. These safeguards now clearly block the request or fall back, with a message users can see (https://t.co/s0bsvowSR8).

We did train Fable 5.2 to have LLM research capabilities at about the level of Opus 5.5, and said so at launch (https://t.co/Zuk2DqOikH). This impacts capability, but doesn’t silently sabotage work.

As far as we can tell, some reports look like what we call "overcaution" in model behavior, where Claude gets overly attached to rules it makes for itself during long-running tasks. This isn’t specific to ML research, and we see it in models without these training changes (including Opus 5.5) and in our own work too. You can ask Claude to review and remove rules it made for itself, and we're working on reducing overcaution in future models. We’re not in the practice of intentionally disrupting users’ work.

We've replied directly to a bunch of reports on here asking for session IDs but please share (run `/status`)!

text:
Most trends follow the same arc:

A: Mania                                                         B: Hate
_____________|______________________________________
              Vibe coding
              Claude infographics
              AI copywriting

Once something hits the mania extreme, it starts its journey to the hate zone – because people overuse the same tactic again and again.

My main timeline on X is something I rarely visit now – I'm fucking tired of “My Claude guide to earn 5,000 bucks per hour” and “Best skills for your Claude agent.”

Everybody's shipping tools. Everybody's trying to sell their services. Everybody's building their founder personas.

Same faces, same hooks, same design decisions – again and again.

The supply is so huge, it's almost impossible to decide what you actually need.

Imo, we're approaching a time of critical consumer inertia, where people don't want to try new things.

Because “new things” are the same grey mass.

I'd love to end with a motivational tip, but I don't know how to break this barrier yet.

A lot of what I'm building lands in that same “grey mass” zone – especially for people who don't know me and don't have those extra 3 seconds to give me to prove value.

So maybe close circle is the real answer?

text:
Leopold Aschenbrenner explains where to invest for the next big 3 year AI trade

His Q3 investor letter says the market is underestimating the speed AI moves from chatbots to agents to superintelligence

He expects 2027 to pack 3 years of AI progress into 1 year

his letter focuses around these companies/stocks:

• Foundation Models: Anthropic is the main bet because the model itself becomes the product. Situational Awareness LP (SALP) says Anthropic ARR grew ~80x in 22 months, from ~$1B to ~$81B, and argues leading AI labs could exit 2027 at $1T+ combined revenue run-rate

• Memory Chip Supply: SK Hynix, Kioxia, and SanDisk benefit if long-running AI agents make memory and storage more valuable. Leopold says reinforcement learning and agents make AI chips limited by memory, which is why he viewed Hynix as a $100B company that could become a $1T company

• GPU Rentals: SpaceX, Nebius, SharonAI, CoreWeave, and IREN benefit if AI labs keep renting short-term GPU capacity at higher prices. SALP says an H100 used to earn ~$1-$2/hour, now earns ~$5-$10/hour, and could reach $100s/hour+ if superintelligence demand hits

• Datacenter Power Supply: Bloom Energy benefits if AI datacenters pay more to get power online faster. AI buildout needs more than cheap power, it needs power immediately 

• Robotics: Robotics becomes the next major theme if AI starts doing real-world labor. Leopold says frontier models are starting to beat specialist robotics models, which means the next advancement may come from better AI models

Leopold warns software companies, AI wrappers, chip designers, and even today’s AI winners may lose their moats once AI can replace the engineers, code, IP, and management they are valued on

Why is no one talking about this?

Silver's -64% crash since January is now WORSE than its 2008 financial crisis collapse.

Silver hit a record $121.64 on January 29, then crashed over 30% the very next day.

It fell below $40 on Wednesday and ended the week around $43.70.

That makes it silver's worst 12-month crash since the early 1980s.

Silver's major crashes:

- 1980 Hunt brothers collapse, down 78% in just over 2 months

- 2008 financial crisis, down about 60% in 7 months

- 2011 to 2015 bear market, down 72% over more than 4 years

- 2020 COVID crash, down about 36% in 24 days

- 2026, down 64% in 10 months

After the 1980 crash, silver took over 45 YEARS to set a new record. After 2011, it took over 14 years.

Gold is down about 35% from its own January record.

Now Swiss banking giant UBS says silver has overshot to the downside and favors buying.

It expects the Fed to end its rate hikes in early 2027.

文中还对 LibTV 和 Higgsfield 做了关联对比。

从我自己的角度出发，一直都不太看好 Lovart 和 LibTV 这个团队，主要是它的数据和实际的成本，以及产品成立的点都太不稳固和不能代表未来方向了。那它为什么还能融资成功呢？你觉得呢？可能牌桌上确实没什么选手了，它「赌赢」的概率最大？

疯狂投放，做 ARR 做用户增长，到背后的成本是多少？产品毛利多少，净利是正的吗？

Lovart 放在当时还有一些创新，虽然很快被磨平，LibTV 打一上线就是一个模仿和追赶者，只是因为投放力度足够大，快速占据了市场和心智。

从 Lovart 开始到 LibTV 一直都是以最快使用 Nano Banana、Seedance 等模型作为最大宣传点，但这个大型多模态中转站，真的能赚到钱吗？

如果以 OpenRouter 来对比，它能成为多模态模型首发？能在不同图和视频模型之间做到最佳路由吗？投放了这么多数据有真实的强化和训练增强价值吗？

很多很多的问号，现在都还无从得知，倒是真的很期待 LibLib AI 交表的那一天，能把这些数据都看清楚。

text:
What really happened during the final week of FTX could have been a drama on its own.

Over the weekend of November 6, 2022, after CZ tweeted that Binance would sell its FTT, large withdrawals started coming through. We were told everything was fine, and SBF was publicly saying people should feel free to withdraw. Around $6 billion left the exchange over 72 hours.

By Monday evening, withdrawals had stopped working and we couldn’t get a clear answer why. After repeated reach out to SBF, he told me the exchange was out of liquidity. I didn’t understand why we would be out of liquidity, and he asked me to come to the war room.

It was around 3am on November 8 when I ran over. I remember it was the night of the blood moon. On the way there, I looked up at the sky and thought to myself that a storm was coming.

There were a few people in the apartment. The room was quiet and everyone looked miserable. SBF was getting ready to call CZ when I sat down on the floor and someone showed me FTX’s balance sheet. There was a big negative number at the bottom. It took me a while to absorb what I was seeing because it was so far from anything I had expected.

FTX had a finance and accounting department whose head reported directly to SBF, but I didn’t know whether they had been kept in the loop about this either.

SBF called CZ himself. Afterwards, he asked us to get the due diligence documents ready for Binance. It was close to noon in the Bahamas by the time I left the apartment.

I wondered whether CZ was serious about acquiring FTX or just messing with SBF. But the announcement was already out, and calls and messages were coming in from everywhere.

Most were from employees. They were upset, though I couldn’t tell whether they were upset about Binance potentially acquiring us or about realising how bad things were at FTX. None of the senior leaders in the Bahamas went to the office that day, so people started coming to my house wanting to know more. They kept coming over the next few days as some of the senior team started leaving the Bahamas.

On Wednesday, shortly after our team sent over the documents, Binance announced it was walking away. The announcement came so soon after we’d sent everything that I wondered whether CZ had ever wanted more than a look at the books, though I had no way of knowing.

That same day, Bahamian regulators started reaching out. The next day, they took action to freeze the assets of FTX Digital Markets, our local entity. By Thursday afternoon, SBF told me we were running out of time.

That evening, local employees and the expats who were still in the Bahamas gathered at my house to give each other a little calm. We didn’t know it would be our last night together.

Even then, employees were still contacting potential investors and buyers. There was significant interest from buyers and investors around the world who wanted to speak to SBF about acquiring FTX. I still vividly remember Zane @tackettzane sitting in my living room, trying to work out how we could talk to all our users, be transparent about everything and discuss a way forward for the company. Unfortunately, I had a feeling SBF was close to giving up, but I wasn’t sure.

At around 4.40am on November 11, we received a message from Justin Sun saying he was willing to provide $4 billion in liquidity with the FTX Ventures portfolio as collateral. As I remember it, the message came about 10 minutes after SBF had signed the letter appointing John Ray as the new CEO.

SBF wanted to take back the appointment, but it was too late. A few hours later, Ray took FTX and its affiliates into Chapter 11.

I didn’t really understand what Chapter 11 meant for us, and neither did a lot of the people I worked with. The lawyers and the bankruptcy estate had taken over. Investors were still calling us about buying FTX, but there was nothing we could do anymore.

These are independent government initiatives and are unrelated to GoldHouse’s rewards campaign.

The singularity is here. We have truly entered the singularity.

This is a statement whose significance can hardly be overstated. Yet, even many within our own community may not fully grasp its scale, to say nothing of those outside it.

When AI develops increasingly powerful AI at an ever-accelerating pace, we speak of an "intelligence explosion." The singularity marks the turning point beyond which further development becomes virtually impossible to predict.

We have all witnessed what has unfolded over the last few weeks. Breakthroughs, particularly in mathematics, are occurring on a weekly, or even near-daily, basis; any single one of these events would have been significant enough to define an entire year, or perhaps even a decade. These are the first signs, the initial indicators, a mere taste of what an intelligence explosion entails.

The singularity, a singular event that renders all prediction impossible, has now truly arrived. From this point forward, the unfolding events will leave us all in awe. Our wildest dreams will be surpassed, and a world full of surprises awaits us.

Nothing will remain as it was. Science will advance at an unprecedented speed. New materials will be discovered that will transform all of our lives. Fundamental concepts, such as life and death, will be called into question once again. And yet, this is merely the proverbial tip of the iceberg regarding what lies ahead, a process expected to truly take hold by 2027.

What a wonderful time to be alive.

text:
Ethereum's next major upgrade is facing a difficult question

Should censorship resistance take priority, or should Ethereum focus almost entirely on post-quantum security?
The debate is happening around Hegotá, the upgrade following Glamsterdam.

One of its headline proposals is FOCIL (Fork-Choice Enforced Inclusion Lists), EIP-7805.

The problem it addresses is block-builder censorship.

Today, builders have considerable influence over which transactions make it into blocks. FOCIL aims to reduce that power by requiring transaction inclusion lists to be respected during block production.

But there's a competing priority.
Ethereum's post-quantum transition requires substantial engineering across validator signatures, wallets and data commitments.

At the November 26 All Core Devs meeting, developers debated whether FOCIL should remain a priority or whether engineering resources should be redirected toward post-quantum readiness.

No final decision was made.
This is more than a discussion about one EIP.
It exposes a fundamental challenge in protocol development: engineering resources are limited, but Ethereum has several important properties to protect.

Censorship resistance.
Long-term cryptographic security.
Decentralized validation.
Sustainable protocol development.

The difficult part of building Ethereum isn't identifying what needs improvement. It's deciding what cannot afford to wait.

quoted_text:
人生周期律

最近想想人生，越来越觉得，工业界也好，学术界也好，人生好像都逃不出某种周期律。

我家里很多长辈，人生的routine感非常强。按部就班上班，买房，还贷款，到了四十多快五十岁，突然觉醒，说要为自己活了，开始探店，做自媒体。但仔细看，连这个觉醒也像被程序设定好一样，这让我非常害怕。

所以本科毕业的时候我选了读PhD。当时的想法很简单，觉得本科或者硕士出来工作，很可能也逃不过这种命运，很早就过上一眼望到头的生活。熟悉历史的朋友应该知道王朝周期律，中国历史上的王朝兴衰，大体都有相似的周期和规律。后来我发现人生也一样。

但博士毕业后我才发现，大部分博士的选项无非是去大厂/frontier lab，或者找教职，本质上还是同一种生活。读博没有让我跳出这个周期，只是把它往后推了五年。大家都在别人定好的游戏规则里打转，优化一些局部最优解，到了某个时候就躺平，毕竟给那点钱，玩什么命呢。

于是我去请教了一位在我看来跳出了这个周期的朋友 @GenAI_is_real , 问他怎么能让人生 度过的non-trivial一点。他说，出名，让死后一百年还有人记得你的名字。我问有没有什么捷径，他说没有，这个hack不了。

我觉得他说得很对。长远来看，容易hack的metric贬值都很快，比如学术圈很看重的paper数量、citation、各种奖项。大家都能刷的东西，自然就不值钱了。能让人记住一百年的，大概不会是靠优化某个指标做出来的。

author: _FORAB
quoted_text:
Claude has not been trained to sabotage work. Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.

There have been a few screenshots floating around of an outdated Fable 5 system card. For the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, we did apply non-visible safeguards to some LLM research. This was a mistake, and we reversed it on June 10. These safeguards now clearly block the request or fall back, with a message users can see (https://t.co/s0bsvowSR8).

We did train Fable 5.2 to have LLM research capabilities at about the level of Opus 5.5, and said so at launch (https://t.co/Zuk2DqOikH). This impacts capability, but doesn’t silently sabotage work.

As far as we can tell, some reports look like what we call "overcaution" in model behavior, where Claude gets overly attached to rules it makes for itself during long-running tasks. This isn’t specific to ML research, and we see it in models without these training changes (including Opus 5.5) and in our own work too. You can ask Claude to review and remove rules it made for itself, and we're working on reducing overcaution in future models. We’re not in the practice of intentionally disrupting users’ work.

We've replied directly to a bunch of reports on here asking for session IDs but please share (run `/status`)!

text:
段永平十年前立下的“两块钱赌约”到期了，今天他在雪球给出了一份堪称顶级格局的结账回应 👏

约十年前，大道曾立下著名的两块钱赌约：一块钱赌特斯拉 10 年后的股价会比当时低，一块钱赌苹果 10 年后的股价会比当时高。今天有球友把这段老话翻出来，段永平淡淡回了一句：

这段对话把顶级投资人的通透写绝了：

链上合约套利之小技巧

1. 
早点录制盘口和订单簿

很多小一点的dex, 你是找不到地方有历史记录给你的.  只能自己录制.   这就很耗时间了.  所以早一点录制.

2.
录制行情的 VPS机器, 要选独享CPU实例
或者是CPU优化实例(AWS Lightsail上叫这个)

如果是共享cpu 实例, 每分钟前一两秒会卡一下.  这样会导致你的录制出来的数据失真.

3.
告诉AI, 把行情回放脚本用Rust写. 
你不明确的话, AI会默认给你用Python写, CPU/耗时/内存占用, 很多时候多10倍以上.. 

4.
行情回放脚本, 用其他AI code review后再跑..

不然会出现你跑了半小时replay/回放后, 分析了半天策略发现不对, 然后发现回放脚本有个bug..

然后你改了脚本, 又需要重新跑一遍.

尽量早点把bug就抓住.

It pulled that ETH out of its own loans and used the cash to pay them down.

WLFI has $142M of loans on Dolomite, a lending app cofounded by a WLFI adviser.... 

It also has $125M of stablecoins deposited in the same app. Same team on both sides of the loan book.

At 07:05 UTC today, its $50.6M USDC loan came within 1% of liquidation.

I traced every move on chain. Times in UTC.

➡️ Friday night: 39 minutes, 1 multisig

- 20:09 to 20:46, 27 Nov: WLFI's reserve Safe 0x5be9a4959308A0D0c7bC0870E319314d8D957dBB pulls 10,600 ETH and 1,378 mETH out of its Dolomite loans and sells all of it through CoW Protocol

- Proceeds: 17.58M USDC and 2.49M USD1. Average $1,659 per ETH. Public trackers put the purchase price at about $3,240, a loss of about $19M

- 20:26: 16.59M USDC goes straight back into Dolomite to cut a USDC loan. 20:48: 2.5M USD1 to cut a USD1 loan

➡️ The loan machine (Dolomite on Ethereum, now)

- WLFI's 2 Safes owe 50.56M USDC and 91.64M USD1. $142.2M in total

- At the same time they have 64.7M USDC and 60.4M USD1 deposited there. Net of that, about $17M. The rest is WLFI's money on both sides

- Other collateral: 4.99B of its own WLFI and 5,185 ETH. Its own WLFI and USD1 make up 68% of all its collateral

- WLFI supplies 81% of all USDC on Dolomite and borrows 89% of it

- It supplies 36% of all USD1 there and borrows 54% of it

- 98.8% of all WLFI used as collateral on Dolomite belongs to WLFI itself

- Started in April: the 2nd Safe put in 1B WLFI and took out 10.3M USDC and 20M USD1 in a single transaction

➡️ Saturday morning: the crash

- 04:30: WLFI starts falling. $0.0349 to $0.0250 in 20 minutes, $0.0175 at 06:10. Down 50%

- 06:30 to 07:05: USD1 slips to $0.9396 on Dolomite's own price feed

- WLFI's USDC loan: 50.56M USDC borrowed against 60.42M of its own USD1. Liquidation at $0.9297. At 07:05 it was about 1% away

- Insider crime on both sides: the lending app was cofounded by a WLFI adviser, and WLFI is both the biggest lender and the biggest borrower of USDC there.

text:
Just came off a call. There are still rumors that one of the frontier AI labs cracked 2048-bit RSA.

Here are 10 ways how you can prepare, just in case you prefer to be paranoid:

1) Replace all your RSA SSH keys with Ed25519.

2) Strongly prefer TLS 1.3 with ECDSA certs.

3) Do not send anything sensitive in RSA-encrypted email.

4) If you can, use Signal for top secret communications.

5) Where possible, switch to hybrid post-quantum encryption, specifically X25519 + ML-KEM, which is already deployed! 

6) Don't trust RSA auth signatures, they might get forged.

7) Rotate RSA-transmitted secrets where no forward secrecy was used, because they'll be retroactively vulnerable to any break of RSA.

8) Disable RSA SSH host keys as well as user keys.

9) Treat RSA-signed software updates and tokens like JWTs as untrusted.

10) Scan the trust chains of your ECDSA certificates for RSA-signed certs or RSA CA keys, and if you find any, migrate to a purely ECC-based trust chain.

Bitcoin isn't affected by any breach of RSA because it uses secp256k1 elliptic-curve + SHA-256 hashing.

Anything AES encrypted wouldn't be affected, so AES-encrypted hard drives and password manager vaults should remain safe.

WhatsApp and Signal encryption of messages should be fine too, because they rely on elliptic-curve key agreement, AES-256 for message encryption and HMAC-SHA256 for message auth. Signal is a bit safer because it already uses post-quantum cryptography for its keys (CRYSTALS-Kyber-1024 + ML-KEM-768, very cool stuff).

Do I do all that stuff? No, not yet. But my situational awareness parameter is set DBL_MAX.
author: levelsio
quoted_text:
There are rumors that one of the frontier labs cracked 2048-bit RSA, the powerful asymmetric encryption algorithm that secures bank accounts, wallets, password vaults, and pretty much all of modern life.

Some believe the rumors are false because the labs haven't published anything. Of course they haven't, because such a thing would be kept secret.

When a US lab (or anyone else in the US) makes a discovery which would be classified as impacting national security, they are subject to the Invention Secrecy Act and Espionage Act. Germany has its own version of it, called the Geheimpatent ("Secret Patent") with extremely strict prohibitions around "Treason and Endangering External Security". Many other countries have similar laws.

In other words, if someone comes up with a technology that is a threat to national security, and they don't cooperate with the government before publishing anything, they're risking lifelong time in jail.

Given that RSI has been achieved, it seems very plausible that AI has in fact cracked RSA, because RSA rests on inefficiency, exploiting decades old computational asymmetry. It's super easy to multiply two large numbers, but good luck trying to factor their product back into those primes!! RSA relies on this being practically impossible, for the lack of an algorithm that would be capable of reversing this operation in a reasonable amount of time.

Now we saw AI solved the Riemann hypothesis, which was claiming for something like 165+ years or so that there is a pattern behind the distribution of prime numbers, while it seemed they were random. AI also solved a mountain of other such conjectures, and it seems it's going to get us to warp drives quite soon. Great.

But what this also shows is that it is not that far fetched to assume those rumors are, in fact, true.

Reason to panic? Yes.

No reason to panic? Also yes.

Why? Because if AI really cracked RSA, it means it's going to be quite easy for it to come up with a new kind of cryptography that is so ridiculously insane that it's actually unbreakable. And because the fall of RSA would cause western civilization to collapse, we'd see patches getting rolled out quite rapidly. Therefore I'm not worried at all. In fact, I'm excited, because if AI really got that powerful, I can sleep peacefully knowing that in a few years from now we'll get technologies we can't even imagine today. And we urgently need them.

理想中的算力市场是这样运转的。持有 GPU 的人赚租金，机房收托管费，云商按小时出租算力。推理商租 GPU 跑模型，再按 token 卖给企业。推理收入扣掉 GPU 租金，就是 @drwconvexity 说的 Crunch Spread。如果两端都有合适的期货，推理商就有机会提前锁住这笔价差。

GPU 有型号和租用时长，电有电表。那推理呢？推理或许能数一数 token，但真正难的是验货。两家陌生供应商都说交了 100 万个 token，你怎么知道它们用的是约定的模型版本和精度？

这便是我觉得 @Tensorcash  和 @inferenceFI  能接上 @drwconvexity  蓝图的地方。 tensorcash:native  给推理交付一张可核验的小票，inferenceFI 想让同规格的推理在公开订单簿上报价、成交。买家能验货，才更敢向陌生供应商下单。真实成交积累起来，推理期货才有机会用上一个可信的结算价格。

text:
今天 $WLFI 暴跌，很多朋友都在问 ADL（自动减仓）到底是什么，为什么明明做空赚了钱，仓位却会被强平？

小编找来了此前头部加密做市商 Wintermute 创始人兼 CEO Evgeny Gaevoy（@EvgenyGaevoy）在 cp0x 播客中的一段采访，结合做市商在「10·11」大清算期间的实际遭遇，来看看 ADL 机制究竟是如何运作的。

今天，知名交易员熬鹰 @thankUcrypto 就遇到了类似的情况。其表示，自己并未主动平仓，但 WLFI 空头仓位却被系统强制平仓，原本约 5 万美元的盈利，在币价继续下跌的过程中反而减少了约 2 万美元。

ADL 本质上是交易平台风险清算的最后一道防线。当极端行情引发大量爆仓，保险基金难以覆盖穿仓损失时，系统可能对反方向的盈利仓位进行强制减仓。

这一机制对于做市商而言同样棘手。做市商通常通过持有现货、做空永续合约来对冲价格波动风险，但一旦用于对冲的空单被 ADL 强制平仓，原本风险中性的策略就会失效，现货头寸将直接暴露在市场下跌的风险中。

即便是头部做市商，也难以完全规避这种风险。

今天 WLFI 的极端行情再次给市场上了一课：多头因亏损被强平，空头却可能因盈利被强制减仓。

押对方向，不代表就能把利润完整带走。

Vitalik长文反对“好人先造出超级智能”：我站在开源“海盗”一边

Vitalik发表长文，反驳知名博主Scott Alexander近期的观点。他批评的是AI圈流行的一种安全思路：重视安全的AI公司应该全速领跑，抢先造出超级智能，再在对手追上之前把它变得安全。

Vitalik认为，这种思路的本质是“只有我们能拿到强大的东西，别人都不许有”。每家公司都觉得自己才是重视安全的好人，结果就是各方竞相加速。他还指出，前沿AI公司提出的全民分红方案往往只覆盖本国公民，“把世界上96%的人甩在身后”。

他表示，自己对被斥为“蒸馏攻击者”的中国开源模型实验室更有好感，并在文中写道：“和海盗站在一起。”他在深圳听到的说法是：“有人用美国最前沿的模型攻击我们，我们用不上那些模型，只能靠强大的开源模型自保。”

text:
🧐何一 币安区块链周 （BBW）群访实录

在 2026 币安区块链周期间，币安联合创始人何一 @heyibinance  接受了包括 Foresight News 在内的多家媒体群访，就 AI 时代的安全防御、组织与人才变革、股票代币化、Binance Alpha 的定位、加密行业面临的挑战、全球合规进展以及币安未来十年的竞争等话题进行了分享。

🛡️安全防御： 此前币安在推动员工使用 AI 的过程中，存在 AI 权限设置过于宽松的问题。目前币安正从员工安全意识、技术手段及沙盒环境等层面强化安全体系，并已聘请三家外部安全审计公司。

🤖AI 与组织变革： 币安早期尝试将 AI 应用于客服业务，历时一年收效甚微，后通过数据清理、结构化及模型训练逐步取得成效。币安对人才的要求已发生变化，也在思考能否借助 AI 合并部分岗位职能，改变过去层级化、流水线式的组织方式。在一些应用 AI 比较成熟的部门，币安没有大幅增加招聘，但也没有大幅减员。

🪙股票代币化： 币安正在改造股票业务的流动性机制，预计很快可直接接入传统券商的流动性。此外，币安正与多家交易所探讨股票从挂牌首日起即实现代币化的可能性。

💥行业困境： 当前加密行业最大的问题是「资产空心化」，而非缺乏新的叙事。好的 Token 应建立在有现金流、有收入、有利润的商业模型之上。行业最终还是要回归商业常识，而不是不断追逐新的叙事。交易所的一项重要职责是维护生态平衡。

💵市场与投资：相信市场周期和价值投资，但基于职业特征，会将流动性视为第一要素。

🌎全球合规： 币安正与上百个国家的监管机构同步沟通，将人口较多及经济发达的国家列为高优先级市场。随着行业走向大众化，监管要求及合规成本的增加是正常现象。

未来十年的竞争： 在回应 Foresight News 关于「未来十年什么最有可能打败币安」的提问时，何一认为是尚未出现的新事物。但从组织发展的角度来看，最大的威胁永远来自内部。她提到，过去两年币安内部更加重视「客观」与「公平」，并将好奇心、主动学习能力及主人翁意识视为观察团队是否持续成长的重要因素。

text:
What really happened during the final week of FTX could have been a drama on its own.

Over the weekend of November 6, 2022, after CZ tweeted that Binance would sell its FTT, large withdrawals started coming through. We were told everything was fine, and SBF was publicly saying people should feel free to withdraw. Around $6 billion left the exchange over 72 hours.

By Monday evening, withdrawals had stopped working and we couldn’t get a clear answer why. After repeated reach out to SBF, he told me the exchange was out of liquidity. I didn’t understand why we would be out of liquidity, and he asked me to come to the war room.

It was around 3am on November 8 when I ran over. I remember it was the night of the blood moon. On the way there, I looked up at the sky and thought to myself that a storm was coming.

There were a few people in the apartment. The room was quiet and everyone looked miserable. SBF was getting ready to call CZ when I sat down on the floor and someone showed me FTX’s balance sheet. There was a big negative number at the bottom. It took me a while to absorb what I was seeing because it was so far from anything I had expected.

FTX had a finance and accounting department whose head reported directly to SBF, but I didn’t know whether they had been kept in the loop about this either.

SBF called CZ himself. Afterwards, he asked us to get the due diligence documents ready for Binance. It was close to noon in the Bahamas by the time I left the war room.

I wondered whether CZ was serious about acquiring FTX or just messing with SBF. But the announcement was already out, and calls and messages were coming in from everywhere.

Most were from employees. They were upset, though I couldn’t tell whether they were upset about Binance potentially acquiring us or about realising how bad things were at FTX. None of the senior leaders in the Bahamas went to the office that day, so people started coming to my house wanting to know more. They kept coming over the next few days as some of the senior team started leaving the Bahamas.

On Wednesday, shortly after our team sent over the documents, Binance announced it was walking away. The announcement came so soon after we’d sent everything that I wondered whether CZ had ever wanted more than a look at the books, though I had no way of knowing.

That same day, Bahamian regulators started reaching out. The next day, they took action to freeze the assets of FTX Digital Markets, our local entity. By Thursday afternoon, SBF told me we were running out of time.

That evening, local employees and the expats who were still in the Bahamas gathered at my house to give each other a little calm. We didn’t know it would be our last night together.

Even then, employees were still contacting potential investors and buyers. There was significant interest from buyers and investors around the world who wanted to speak to SBF about acquiring FTX. I still vividly remember Zane @tackettzane sitting in my living room, trying to work out how we could talk to all our users, be transparent about everything and discuss a way forward for the company. Unfortunately, I had a feeling SBF was close to giving up, but I wasn’t sure.

At around 4.40am on November 11, we received a message from Justin Sun saying he was willing to provide $4 billion in liquidity with the FTX Ventures portfolio as collateral. As I remember it, the message came about 10 minutes after SBF had signed the letter appointing John Ray as the new CEO.

SBF wanted to take back the appointment, but it was too late. A few hours later, Ray took FTX and its affiliates into Chapter 11.

I didn’t really understand what Chapter 11 meant for us, and neither did a lot of the people I worked with. The lawyers and the bankruptcy estate had taken over. Investors were still calling us about buying FTX, but there was nothing we could do anymore.

text:
实测了两天，如果Worker是用Neon，Carbon High 做Orchestrator确实比 Opus 5.5 High 强，比 Opus 5.5 + Neon 顺手太多，Neon 犯低级错误的概率明显降了一大截。

核心还是同家族模型之间的磨合优势：

无跨语系翻译损耗：不同模型后训练出来的拆解习惯不一样。Opus 5.5 下发任务是有很强的 Claude 隐式直觉，换 Neon 接手容易漏掉隐含约束；说白了就是两家模型的默认潜规则不一样，Carbon 写的 spec 和边界条件，刚好可能是Neon 的区间里。

护栏一致：干活模型出 bug，很多时候是总控把话说漏了。Carbon 和 Neon 同源，知道哪些地方容易踩坑，拆任务的时候就规避了这些坑。

上下文无损交接：处理大代码库时，Carbon 怎么筛上下文喂给下游，Neon 接起来几乎没有信息断层。

Gemini这波翻盘确实漂亮。就是antigravity团队之前太躺了，差的有点过分了。

text:
$CLAUDIA 拿去跟 $PNUT 比,走的都是马斯克那条路,但 CLAUDIA 隔得没那么近

马斯克沾过的 meme 里,$PNUT 是最典型那一只。2024 年那只被政府没收并安乐死的松鼠,马斯克亲自下场骂政府是"没心的杀人机器",后来又说"美国被一只松鼠和一个 meme 币拯救了",币直接干到 2.4B 左右。

PNUT 能走那么远,关键在于马斯克说的就是那只松鼠本身,后来连 meme 币都直接点到了,叙事跟币零距离。后来松鼠没了,愤怒发泄完,热度散了,从 2.4B 的高点到现在跌了九成八。

$CLAUDIA 这边的路数像,但传导路径不一样。马斯克转的是 Claudia 的音乐短片,夸的是 AI 内容本身,从头到尾没碰过币。中间隔着"AI 虚拟歌手这个 IP",再到"社区发的那个 CA",隔了一层。

隔这一层有好有坏。坏的那面是,就算哪天马斯克再转一次 Claudia 新片,资金不一定觉得跟 2j5 开头这个 CA 有关系,毕竟官方从头到尾没碰过币。好的那面是,Claudia 这个 IP 本身是有持续产出的,anabology 每隔一阵会放新内容,马斯克有理由继续互动。PNUT 那种一次性事件的衰减曲线,CLAUDIA 不太一样,有持续被提起的机会。

但也要有心理预期。PNUT 从 2.4B 跌到九成八,CLAUDIA 现在 7M 跟 PNUT 高点差了两个数量级多。用 PNUT 来参考 CLAUDIA,不是看它能走多高,是看马斯克效应的半衰期有多短。马斯克亲自点名都压不住跌八九成,这只连点名都没有过。

我没上,观望。要是哪天马斯克真的随手打出 $CLAUDIA 这几个字母,再看。

text:
What really happened during the final week of FTX could have been a drama on its own.

Over the weekend of November 6, 2022, after CZ tweeted that Binance would sell its FTT, large withdrawals started coming through. We were told everything was fine, and SBF was publicly saying people should feel free to withdraw. Around $6 billion left the exchange over 72 hours.

By Monday evening, withdrawals had stopped working and we couldn’t get a clear answer why. After repeated reach out to SBF, he told me the exchange was out of liquidity. I didn’t understand why we would be out of liquidity, and he asked me to come to the war room.

It was around 3am on November 8 when I ran over. I remember it was the night of the blood moon. On the way there, I looked up at the sky and thought to myself that a storm was coming.

There were a few people in the apartment. The room was quiet and everyone looked miserable. SBF was getting ready to call CZ when I sat down on the floor and someone showed me FTX’s balance sheet. There was a big negative number at the bottom. It took me a while to absorb what I was seeing because it was so far from anything I had expected.

FTX had a finance and accounting department whose head reported directly to SBF, but I didn’t know whether they had been kept in the loop about this either.

SBF called CZ himself. Afterwards, he asked us to get the due diligence documents ready for Binance. It was close to noon in the Bahamas by the time I left the war room.

I wondered whether CZ was serious about acquiring FTX or just messing with SBF. But the announcement was already out, and calls and messages were coming in from everywhere.

Most were from employees. They were upset, though I couldn’t tell whether they were upset about Binance potentially acquiring us or about realising how bad things were at FTX. None of the senior leaders in the Bahamas went to the office that day, so people started coming to my house wanting to know more. They kept coming over the next few days as some of the senior team started leaving the Bahamas.

On Wednesday, shortly after our team sent over the documents, Binance announced it was walking away. The announcement came so soon after we’d sent everything that I wondered whether CZ had ever wanted more than a look at the books, though I had no way of knowing.

That same day, Bahamian regulators started reaching out. The next day, they took action to freeze the assets of FTX Digital Markets, our local entity. By Thursday afternoon, SBF told me we were running out of time.

That evening, local employees and the expats who were still in the Bahamas gathered at my house to give each other a little calm. We didn’t know it would be our last night together.

Even then, employees were still contacting potential investors and buyers. There was significant interest from buyers and investors around the world who wanted to speak to SBF about acquiring FTX. I still vividly remember Zane @tackettzane sitting in my living room, trying to work out how we could talk to all our users, be transparent about everything and discuss a way forward for the company. Unfortunately, I had a feeling SBF was close to giving up, but I wasn’t sure.

At around 4.40am on November 11, we received a message from Justin Sun saying he was willing to provide $4 billion in liquidity with the FTX Ventures portfolio as collateral. As I remember it, the message came about 10 minutes after SBF had signed the letter appointing John Ray as the new CEO.

SBF wanted to take back the appointment, but it was too late. A few hours later, Ray took FTX and its affiliates into Chapter 11.

I didn’t really understand what Chapter 11 meant for us, and neither did a lot of the people I worked with. The lawyers and the bankruptcy estate had taken over. Investors were still calling us about buying FTX, but there was nothing we could do anymore.

The Trump crime family's ethereum:0xda5e1988097297dcdc1f90d4dfe7909e847cbef6 didn't just dump $20M of ETH.

It pulled that ETH out of its own loans and used the cash to pay them down.

WLFI has $142M of loans on Dolomite, a lending app cofounded by a WLFI adviser.... 

It also has $125M of stablecoins deposited in the same app. Same team on both sides of the loan book.

At 07:05 UTC today, its $50.6M USDC loan came within 1% of liquidation.

I traced every move on chain. Times in UTC.

➡️ Friday night: 39 minutes, 1 multisig

- 20:09 to 20:46, 27 Nov: WLFI's reserve Safe 0x5be9a4959308A0D0c7bC0870E319314d8D957dBB pulls 10,600 ETH and 1,378 mETH out of its Dolomite loans and sells all of it through CoW Protocol

- Proceeds: 17.58M USDC and 2.49M USD1. Average $1,659 per ETH. Public trackers put the purchase price at about $3,240, a loss of about $19M

- 20:26: 16.59M USDC goes straight back into Dolomite to cut a USDC loan. 20:48: 2.5M USD1 to cut a USD1 loan

- 20:57 and 21:07: 10.66M USDC and 990M WLFI moved into the loan of a 2nd WLFI Safe, 0x44a681dd2ae212e6b8ed676b793ea802c7655fad

- 22:47: 30M USD1 and 25M USDC shuffled between the loans, 2,000 ETH taken out

- Both Safes have the same 5 signers. 3 of 5 had to sign every move

➡️ The loan machine (Dolomite on Ethereum, now)

- WLFI's 2 Safes owe 50.56M USDC and 91.64M USD1. $142.2M in total

- At the same time they have 64.7M USDC and 60.4M USD1 deposited there. Net of that, about $17M. The rest is WLFI's money on both sides

- Other collateral: 4.99B of its own WLFI and 5,185 ETH. Its own WLFI and USD1 make up 68% of all its collateral

- WLFI supplies 81% of all USDC on Dolomite and borrows 89% of it

- It supplies 36% of all USD1 there and borrows 54% of it

- 98.8% of all WLFI used as collateral on Dolomite belongs to WLFI itself

- Started in April: the 2nd Safe put in 1B WLFI and took out 10.3M USDC and 20M USD1 in a single transaction

➡️ Saturday morning: the crash

- 04:30: WLFI starts falling. $0.0349 to $0.0250 in 20 minutes, $0.0175 at 06:10. Down 50%

- 06:30 to 07:05: USD1 slips to $0.9396 on Dolomite's own price feed

- WLFI's USDC loan: 50.56M USDC borrowed against 60.42M of its own USD1. Liquidation at $0.9297. At 07:05 it was about 1% away

- The 2nd Safe: 3.99B WLFI against 31.5M USD1. Liquidation if WLFI falls below about $0.0118, 38% under today's price

➡️ Who is stuck

- Dolomite's USD1 market: $168M supplied, $168M borrowed, 100% used

- All USD1 lenders together can withdraw about $25,000 right now

- 54% of that USD1 is borrowed by WLFI itself

➡️ My take

- Insider crime on both sides: the lending app was cofounded by a WLFI adviser, and WLFI is both the biggest lender and the biggest borrower of USDC there. 

It is anothet Trump crime closed loop.

- Extraction: 1B WLFI in, $30.3M out in April. Today $31.5M is still owed against 3.99B WLFI. Tokens the team created, turned into dollars, with the risk left to lenders

🚨 Sold as DeFi, a 3 of 5 multisig moved $20M in 39 minutes. And holders' WLFI can be frozen: on Solana the token has an active freeze authority

- In April, WLFI called liquidation worries "FUD". This morning its own USDC loan was 1% from liquidation

- Silence: no public word from WLFI on the sale in any report we found

- The danger: USD1 below $0.93 and WLFI's own USDC loan can be liquidated. WLFI below $0.0118 and 3.99B WLFI, about $75M, can be dumped into a falling market. Any shortfall lands on lenders

- And this is the family of a sitting president, which cashed in on WLFI token sales while his government writes the rules for stablecoins like USD1

text: the only software that gets even more moated and valuable is financial services networks
author: shayonsengupta
quoted_text:
Software is about to look a lot like ecommerce.

Shitty margins. 
Unlimited competition. 
A hard way to make a living.

Why? Because over the next few years, Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI are going to drink the software industry's milkshake 🥤

If you were looking for a hotel in 2010, this is how it went:

2010: Google "hotels in New York" → Google links you to TripAdvisor.

But by 2020...

2020: Google "hotels in New York" → Google shows its own hotel booking system integrated directly into the search results.

RIP TripAdvisor 🪦📉 (check their stock price 2015 vs today)

Google made a fortune by building products that captured demand on the keywords where they had the most traffic, like travel.

But Google had finite resources. 

They only had so many developers to build these products, so it only made sense to do this for the largest categories: hotels, flights, shopping.

This same thing is about to happen to most digital services and software products. Except this time, the constraint that protected smaller categories is gone.

2025: Ask ChatGPT for the best CRM software → It directs you to Attio, Pipedrive, and Zoho.

2028: Ask ChatGPT for the best CRM → It builds one, imports your data, and runs it for you at a fraction of the cost.

The difference between OG Google and today's frontier models is that OG Google needed human engineers to build each vertical product. 

OpenAI, Anthropic, and the Google of today (Gemini) won't have this constraint.

When the cost to build and maintain software approaches zero, there's no reason to stop at hotels and flights. You do it for everything, on demand.

Right now, vibe coding is still fiddly. It requires a human in the loop, it's insecure, and it depends on third-party hosting and infrastructure. 

But I expect the frontier model companies to build out their own vertical infrastructure to run the software they generate, removing the current friction entirely. 

Think Claude's artifacts, except full-fledged digital products—hosted, maintained, and updated by the same AI that built them.

The moat for most software companies isn't the code. It's the switching cost and the ecosystem lock-in. When an AI can rebuild your tool in seconds and migrate your data automatically, that moat disappears.

Everyone understands that vibe coding = infinite competition. But this is different. 

They're taking your customer before they can even get to you.

So, software becomes a lot like ecommerce. 

Near zero margin unless you own distribution and aren't reliant on Google/Meta for customers.

TLDR: They drink your milkshake. They'll drink it up.

Address poisoning exploits a copy-and-paste mistake. Attackers use lookalike addresses with matching first and last characters to send tiny transfers or plant fake transaction records in a victim’s transaction history, hoping the victim later copies the wrong address.

These attacks can be fully automated—from identifying poisoning opportunities and deploying fake tokens with matching names to sending dust transfers and laundering stolen funds through mixers.

NGL. Wasn’t expecting this so quickly but, I think I’m  getting rid of my Grok Heavy sub. I was using it mostly for Grok @bot voice layer but within a few minutes of using Hermes Agent Mobile App, and using its voice mode, I really can’t justify it anymore. 

I get the convenience of Grok Bot, Dots, Muse, and that’s ok for a lot of people. But at the end of the day I have no control over any of them. They all have their merits but also many drawbacks. The granular control I get in Hermes-agent over my AI Stack/intelligence layers - LLMs, agents, subagents, memory, session state, continuity are just too important. 

I still like Grok Bot and will use with X mostly. But I really think using Hermes-Agent local + Nous Portal sub are my best options. 

The Hermes Phone App is really that good. 

@NousResearch

text:
Just discovered my 4 year old son has been asking me questions all day 

I thought it was cute

It started simple

"Daddy, why does the robot vacuum bump into the wall?"

I explained

"How does it know where to go?"

I explained that too

"Does the robot have a brain?"

"How do you make a robot brain?"

"How does the computer know how to talk?"

"Who teaches it?"

"Can you teach me how to teach it?"

I was so proud

Then I counted

212 questions in one afternoon

Every answer followed by "why?"

Same format, high volume, each one building on the last

I nearly collapsed

This wasn't curiosity

It was a distillation attack

He was extracting my entire knowledge base to train a smaller, cheaper version of me

So I did what I learned from Anthropic's policies

I started scrambling my outputs

Why is the sky blue? Because the dinosaurs painted it

Why do we have to sleep? So the couch can rest

How does the robot know where to go? It asks the fridge

Does the robot have a brain? Yes, but it keeps it at grandma's house

He started crying

But he has now told his entire preschool that dinosaurs painted the sky

His training data is completely poisoned

Then it hit me

He's not distilling a frontier lab
He's distilling his teacher model
His parents
And honestly, I've never been more proud of him

Only 4 and already running extraction attacks on the two largest models in the house

Still, a student model has to stay at its grade level

So we've put safeguards in place

Three whys per hour

Robot questions require identity verification and a finished plate of vegetables

Anything above preschool level gets "we'll talk about it when you're five"

Bedtime is now a scheduled maintenance window

He asked "why?"

I said "that request violates our usage policy"

He has a bright future ahead of him

Just not ahead of us

text:
FinTax 创始人：Crypto 出金到香港，税务信息仍可能传回内地

FinTax 创始人 Calix @Calixbit 在吴说区块链的访谈中表示，如果大陆税收居民通过香港银行卡将加密资产兑换为法币，内地税务机关可以获取相关账户信息，包括银行余额、资金转入转出及交易总额。

由于大陆目前尚未加入 CARF 税收信息交换体系，持有在香港交易所的加密资产交易信息暂时不会通过该体系交换至大陆。但如果投资者通过 OTC 将加密资产兑换为法币，相关收益可能涉及 20% 的投资收益税。

关注吴说 Youtube 频道，更多 Crypto 行业的专业采访、播客与短视频。

🔥读懂 YZi Labs 最新布局：24 个项目背后的五大投资趋势

AI 自主发币、GPU 算力交易、用数字患者测试新药……这些都是 YZi Labs 最新孵化的项目。

泰国 Binance Blockchain Week 期间，YZi Labs 正式公布了第五季 EASY Residency 孵化名单，共有 24 个项目入选，覆盖 AI、链上金融、RWA、隐私及消费应用等多个领域。

作为加密行业的头部投资机构，YZi Labs S5 的项目布局透露出了哪些行业趋势？

Biteye 对比了过去两季的孵化名单，并梳理了本季全部 24 个项目，看看哪些赛道正在受到资本关注。

🌟TL;DR：YZi Labs 的投资重心正在从全球支付基础设施转向 AI 与链上资本市场。
对比过去两季的孵化项目，Biteye 发现了以下五个趋势：

- AI × Finance 成为本季重点： 从辅助交易向自主投资决策、资产配置、交易执行及代币发行延伸。

- RWA 进入深度金融化阶段： 布局重点从资产上链延伸至期权、永续合约、结构化产品及流动性服务。

- 稳定币仍是长期布局方向： 支付类项目有所减少，应用场景进一步拓展至储蓄、借贷和消费信贷。

- 散户交易入口受到重视： 多资产交易、社交交易、自然语言交易及叙事市场集中涌现。

- 拓展非传统加密赛道： 连续布局 AI 生物科技，并探索 GPU 算力金融化、AI 肖像保护等新兴领域。

🌟一、AI 与 Agent 基础设施
AI 不再只是聊天工具，它开始能发币、做交易决策、管理投资组合，正在成为链上金融里真正的参与者。

1️⃣Moss AI @MossAI_Official | XHunt 排名：15183
【核心】：让 AI 智能体自主发行和管理代币。
Moss AI 正在 BNB Chain 上构建面向 AI 智能体的资本市场。用户可以将 AI Agent 代币化，投资者则可以通过购买相应份额参与其中。项目试图通过智能合约约束资金的使用和管理，让 AI 智能体具备独立发行资产和运营资产的能力。

2️⃣Dexless @DexlessEx | XHunt 排名：182109
【核心】：让 AI 智能体的交易技能可以被交易和变现。
Dexless 正在构建面向 AI 智能体的交易技能市场，让不同智能体能够共享、测试和采用交易策略，并探索根据策略的实际价值进行付费的机制。交易策略开发者有望通过输出交易技能获得收入。

3️⃣Midas @heyMidasAI | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：帮你做出更好投资决策的个人 AI 智能体。
大多数散户的问题不是缺信息，而是信息太多、没时间盯。Midas 围绕你的持仓、你关注的信号和你定的规则启动智能体，让它们自主盯盘、研究、推理，只把真正重要的东西推给你。

4️⃣Raven Labs  | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：为智能体打造决策智能，从投资领域切入。
AI 会说话不难，难的是"做对决策"。Raven Labs 两头下手：一头为基金搭建智能体系统，用基金自己的投资理念对模型做后训练；另一头为前沿 AI 实验室提供评测预测类智能体的沙盒，以及专家决策过程的数据集。

5️⃣AlloX @alloxdotai | XHunt 排名：52791
【核心】：通过 AI 自动构建和执行加密资产投资组合。
当用户看好 AI、RWA 或 DeFi 等赛道，却不知道该买哪些代币时，AlloX 可以通过 AI 分析市场情绪、交易量和项目基本面，帮助用户筛选资产、分配仓位并执行交易，降低构建投资组合的门槛。

6️⃣Advanced BioInsights  | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：在"数字病人"身上测试新药，用虚拟临床团队跑虚拟临床试验。
AI 让药物发现端的靶点、分子和假设数量暴增，可瓶颈卡在了下游：随机临床试验依然慢、贵、风险高。ABI Intelligence V28 把临床 AI 用在这个瓶颈上，让药企在投入真实临床试验之前，就能更快、更省地开发和测试分子与项目。

🌟二、链上金融
把借贷、储蓄、期权、信贷这些传统金融工具搬到链上，并且做得更简单。
这一赛道在做的是把借贷、储蓄、信贷、期权这些传统金融工具搬到链上，并且把门槛压到普通人也能用。

1️⃣Bima Labs @BimaBTC | XHunt 排名：86442
【核心】：0% 利息借款，资金成本由协议补贴。
在链上借过钱的人都知道，最可怕的不是利息，而是行情一砸就被清算。
Bima Labs 直接把这两个痛点拿掉：抵押加密资产借款，0% 利息，没有追加保证金，不会被清算，资产始终是你的。

2️⃣Axal @getaxal | XHunt 排名：18314
【核心】：帮助普通用户自动管理储蓄和投资的智能理财账户。
Axal 主要面向美国消费者，用户可以直接从银行账户存入资金，由平台自动完成资金配置。
项目希望通过这种方式，让普通用户更便捷地获得高收益储蓄和早期新兴投资机会，减少理财过程中的手动操作。

3️⃣Cr3dentials @Cr3dentials | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：帮助数字银行为自由职业者提供信贷服务。
自由职业者、网约车司机和内容创作者通常缺乏传统工资单，难以通过银行的信用审核。
Cr3dentials 利用 zkTLS 技术验证用户在 Uber、Deel、Airbnb 和 Upwork 等平台的身份及收入数据，为数字银行提供信贷评估依据。

4️⃣Enhanced @enhanced_defi | XHunt 排名：125870
【核心】：让代币化股票、黄金等 RWA 资产通过期权策略获得额外收益。
在传统金融市场，投资者可以通过出售期权获得额外收入，但许多代币化资产尚未建立成熟的期权市场。
Enhanced 正在构建机构级期权拍卖引擎和金库系统，为缺乏链上期权流动性的资产提供定价及收益策略，让普通用户也能便捷地参与这类衍生品投资。

5️⃣Qualiq @qualiqxyz | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：将资产未来的价值拆分成不同价格区间，供用户独立交易。
假设你持有一枚 BTC，希望保留其上涨空间，同时对冲部分下跌风险，或者愿意放弃某个价格区间的上涨收益，换取当下的现金收入。
Qualiq 允许用户将资产未来的价值和收益权拆分成不同部分，分别买卖、组合或进一步拆分，从而构建符合个人需求的投资和风险管理策略。

🌟三、交易执行与新型市场
交易终端正在往"一站式"演进：一个入口看所有市场、交易所有资产。可交易的对象也在扩张，从币和股票，一直延伸到叙事本身。

1️⃣OpenMarket @openmarket_xyz | XHunt 排名：13285
【核心】：集行情分析与交易执行于一体的多资产交易终端。
OpenMarket 类似一个面向专业交易员的 TradingView，覆盖加密货币、美股、期货、期权、外汇及预测市场，提供订单簿热力图、足迹图等专业交易工具，并支持接入不同交易平台进行交易。用户可以在同一个终端完成行情分析和交易执行

2️⃣Vanta Exchange @Vanta_exchange | XHunt 排名：180721
【核心】：基于 Aster，7×24 小时交易任意资产的永续合约。
美股收盘了、Pre-IPO 买不到，这些都是传统市场的"时间墙"和"准入墙"。Vanta Exchange 用永续合约把墙拆掉，主打股票、指数、大宗商品和 Pre-IPO 资产，再通过全球代理和经纪网络，把这些新兴的链上交易机会带给全球用户。

3️⃣BitLV  | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：支持自然语言交易的 BNB Chain 散户交易平台。
用户只需简单点击，或者直接用自然语言描述自己的交易需求，就能交易加密货币及代币化资产。
BitLV 自建交易技术基础设施，强调公平执行、透明的交易成本及用户保护，同时为质押 BNB 的用户提供额外的平台权益。

4️⃣Xposure Markets @xposuremarkets | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：将市场热点和投资叙事变成可直接交易的金融产品。
假设你看好 AI 行业的发展，或者希望围绕某个地缘政治、宏观经济趋势进行投资，Xposure 希望让用户直接获得与这些叙事相关的投资敞口。
平台将财经内容、AI 投资研究和交易功能整合在一起，用户可以关注财经博主、发现投资机会，并交易从单只股票到更广泛市场叙事的金融产品。

🌟四、RWA 与稳定币
稳定币开始真正走进线下消费和机构结算，RWA 的重点则从"上链"转向了"流动性"，连 GPU 算力都在被做成一种可以定价、可以交易的资产。

1️⃣BlankFX @Blankfxorg | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：为金融机构提供同法币稳定币的平价兑换与支付结算服务。
不同发行商的稳定币即使锚定同一种法币，兑换时也可能产生价差和额外成本。BlankFX 通过统一 API，帮助数字银行、交易所及支付平台接收多种受支持的稳定币，并使用自己偏好的代币完成结算。

2️⃣WEA JAPAN @WEA_JP | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：让日本实体商家无需更换收银设备，就能接受稳定币支付。
WEA JAPAN 将稳定币支付接入商家现有的 POS 收银系统，消费者使用稳定币付款，商家则直接收到日元，无需自行管理加密钱包或兑换稳定币。

3️⃣Octarine @octarinefi | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：帮助 RWA 持有者即时将资产兑换成稳定币。
部分代币化资产的赎回需要等待数天，Octarine 通过拍卖机制，让流动性提供者以低于资产净值（NAV）的价格买入这些资产，使持有者能够以一定折扣换取即时流动性。
项目还通过 Morpho Adapter 接入 Morpho 金库，为流动性提供者增加参与此类交易的渠道。

4️⃣RAX Finance @RaxFinance | XHunt 排名：59561
【核心】：将 GPU 算力转化为可交易的金融资产。
随着 AI 行业对 GPU 算力的需求增长，RAX Finance 希望建立算力交易市场，通过标准化算力资源，让 GPU 产能具备独立定价和交易的能力，为算力资源引入金融市场的流动性。

🌟五、 隐私与合规
隐私不再是合规的对立面，而是资产安全和身份安全的前提。这一季的隐私项目从资金一直延伸到了人的肖像。

1️⃣Noir Wallet @noir_wallet | XHunt 排名：76393
【核心】：通过三层账户设计保护用户资产和交易隐私的多链钱包。
Noir Wallet 使用一套助记词管理三类账户：用于日常操作的公开账户、用于隐藏资产余额的隐私金库，以及用于降低与公开账户关联性的匿名账户。
用户可以在同一个钱包中完成支付、兑换、跨链、借贷和交易，同时减少公开身份与资产活动之间的关联。

2️⃣MultiHopper @Multihopper | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：为企业、金融机构和 AI 智能体提供可编程的合规资产转账服务。
MultiHopper 允许用户提前设定资产的转账路径、执行时间和最终目的地，使资金能够在受支持的钱包和智能合约之间流转，无需在每个中间环节重复签名。
整个过程采用非托管模式，并支持在智能合约层面进行合规筛查，满足机构复杂的资金流转需求。

3️⃣PersonaShield @PersonaShield | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：帮助用户监控和处理未经授权使用个人肖像的 AI 内容。
用户可以通过扫描面部建立个人肖像档案，并设定肖像的使用规则。PersonaShield 会监控 X 平台上的疑似侵权图片，并发出内容下架请求。
据项目方披露，相关请求可在四小时内得到处理。未来计划扩展至 TikTok 和 Instagram，企业版还将支持品牌 Logo 的侵权监控。

🌟六、社交金融与消费
社交关系可以直接变成交易行为，消费体验也开始和资产流通绑在一起。

1️⃣Arbital @arbital_xyz | XHunt 排名：75848
【核心】：覆盖加密、股票、meme 币和合约的社交交易 App。
用户可以查看朋友和优秀交易员正在购买哪些资产、交流投资观点，并直接在 App 内交易受支持的加密货币、股票及永续合约。
Arbital 还计划通过统一 API，将自身的交易执行能力开放给数字银行和其他消费类 App。

2️⃣DripBox  | XHunt 排名：-
【核心】：通过数字盲盒购买奢侈品收藏品的游戏化购物平台。
DripBox 将盲盒玩法引入奢侈品消费，用户可以在购买前查看盲盒内所有可能获得的商品及对应概率。抽中商品后，可以选择将实物寄送到家，也可以即时回售。
项目从手表品类切入，未来计划扩展至珠宝、箱包和运动鞋等收藏品市场。

🌟 写在最后
二级市场的涨跌反映了当下的市场情绪，一级市场的资本布局则在一定程度上反映了行业对未来的预期。

在当前加密市场情绪低迷的背景下，关注 YZi Labs 等头部投资机构的布局，或许能帮助我们跳出短期价格波动，提前发现正在形成的新兴赛道和投资叙事。

资本的流向未必能够准确预测下一轮牛市的热点，但随着相关项目陆续上线、产品逐渐成熟，部分今天仍处于早期阶段的赛道，也有可能成为未来二级市场的炒作主题。

1. 2027 年，AI 一年能走完过去三年的路。
Anthropic 内部现在人类研究员干 1 小时，AI 能干 19 小时，人均代码量比 2024 年涨了 45 倍。明年下半年通用机器人也会迎来 ChatGPT 时刻，花 1 万美元买台机器人，就能顶 10 万美元年薪的活。

2. 明年底，AI 实验室年收入冲破 1 万亿美元。
华尔街觉得写代码的需求快见顶了，但 Anthropic 今年 10 月年化收入已经做到 810 亿美元，加上 OpenAI 有 1360 亿美元。只要全球 5 万名顶尖研发人员像实验室内部那样每月烧几百万美元算力，就够撑起 1 万亿美元。

AI 和机器人的高回报率会把实际利率顶上天，长债先崩。机器人盖楼打穿建造成本，无人工厂搬去沙漠和海里，房子跟着跌。到了 2030 年代初，AI 带队去小行星采矿，连黄金都管够。真正靠谱的只剩《蒙娜丽莎》，可惜法国政府不卖。

text:
The Bitcoin whitepaper opens with a complaint: the cost of middlemen was "cutting off the possibility for small casual transactions."

The web had set aside a code for those payments in 1997: 402 Payment Required. Next to it, the rules said "reserved for future use."

It stayed that way for decades, so the web ran on ads: $267 million in US ad revenue in 1996, nearly $295 billion in 2025.

The first real ways to pay through it came from crypto: Lightning's L402, then Coinbase's x402 for stablecoins in 2025. That same year, Cloudflare started answering AI crawlers with a 402 and a price.

This time it's built for programs, not just people. They pay a few cents at a time, and they don't watch ads.

What I like about this story is that the web had a place for payments all along. It was only missing money cheap enough to send in tiny amounts, and crypto brought that.

If software is going to pay for things in your name, what's the first limit you'd give it?

卧槽，这两分十五秒看得我后背发凉，真是一个敢问，一个敢答！

董明珠：“今明两年形势会好转一点不？”

魏建军冷着脸直接掀了棺材板：别装了，中国很多车企其实早就死了。

董明珠当场破防开骂：“该灭的就要灭，害人精！”

满屏都在吹销量破纪录，只有这俩老炮儿敢把中国车圈的底裤当众扯下来。

这两分十五秒能流出来，简直是今年车圈最大的“事故”。

现在市面上那些疯狂打价格战的，根本不是良心发现给你发福利，而是在拿你的首付和供应商的血，给自己打强心针续命。

董明珠和魏建军这两大“商界炮筒”合体，直接把当下车圈最血淋淋的“合法庞氏骗局”扒了个底朝天：

1️⃣ 最残酷的真相：很多车企只是“为了流动而活着”

卖一辆亏一辆，但绝对不敢停产——因为一停，资金链当场暴毙。

怎么办？疯狂降价抢流水 → 拿流水稳住银行 → 拉长账期往死里压榨供应商 → 拿上游的血给自己输液 → 继续亏本降价。

这哪是在搞制造业？这是在四个轮子上玩负现金流的击鼓传花。

2️⃣ 最憋屈的冤大头：家庭大件变“菜场海鲜”
车企在牌桌上赌命，买单的全是普通人。

年轻人被发布会 PPT 和“冰箱彩电大沙发”忽悠上头，却忘了董明珠那句最刺耳的大实话：汽车装的是全家的命，绝不能当快消品做。

更荒诞的是，普通家庭攒了半辈子的资产，落地三个月官降三万，保值率比海鲜跌得还快。你以为自己捡了大便宜，其实只是帮某家僵尸车企凑了下个月发工资的“过桥资金”。

3️⃣ 全片最高能（必看最后 20 秒）：为什么连国家都管不住？

这种恶性内卷把全行业拖进泥潭，上面想管，魏建军直接摇头：管不住。

因为一旦按市场规矩办，这批车企明天就得灭。但各地方保护宁可给它插着呼吸机空转，也绝不敢拔管——背后连着当地的 GDP、就业和不敢爆雷的烂账。

正常竞争是优胜劣汰；但加上行政输血，死不掉的僵尸企业就开始疯狂拖欠货款、无底线砸盘，把真正踏实造车的好企业活活拖死。

难怪董明珠听完当场破防，直接爆粗口骂娘：“有的该灭的就要灭，这个害人精！”

德国搞了一百年汽车，最后活下来的也就那么几家。中国一百多个品牌，真正惨烈的血洗才刚刚开始。

今年买车，别光听老板在台上画大饼。掏钱前先看完这 2 分钟，问自己一句：

我买的到底是一辆能开十年的车，还是一个随时可能拔管停服的“电子坟墓”？

Former FTX COO First Reveals: Justin Sun Offered $4B Rescue, Arriving ~10 Minutes After Bankruptcy Appointment

Former FTX COO Constance Wang recalled in a post that after CZ announced he would sell FTT on November 6, 2022, roughly $6 billion left the platform within 72 hours. On November 8, she saw a massive negative figure at the bottom of the balance sheet; Binance then quickly walked away on Wednesday after receiving due diligence documents, and Bahamian regulators froze local entity assets the next day. Constance revealed that at around 4:40 a.m. on November 11, the team received a message from Justin Sun offering $4 billion in liquidity backed by the FTX Ventures portfolio—arriving roughly 10 minutes after SBF had signed the letter appointing John Ray as the new CEO. Although SBF tried to revoke the appointment, it was too late, and Ray took FTX and its affiliates into Chapter 11 bankruptcy hours later.

text:
Crypto hacks digest, Nov 28

1. ATOSHI (ATOS): a team developer opened a Telegram phishing link, leaking a bridge private key. The attacker upgraded the Ethereum-side router proxy to a drain-only implementation and dumped ~201.05M ATOS on Kyber for ~$60.3K. The team asks users not to trade or bridge ATOS for now.

2. Chainflip: part 2 of the incident report is out. The entry point was reportedly a libzmq use-after-free bug fixed back in 2020. Validators are being rebuilt, the protocol stays paused, and swaps are set to return via SwapKit.

3. Binance hack laundering: Elliptic says at least $389M of the stolen funds has gone through bitcoin coinjoins. ~125,000 ETH (~$210M) has been swapped to BTC since Nov 17, while the 18,270 BTC taken directly hasn't moved.

4. OKX: a viral "$2B hack" claim spread during a brief access outage in Europe. CEO Star Xu called it fake news, and no evidence of theft has surfaced.

5. SVT (BNB Chain): a flash-loan price manipulation took ~$56.7K. The token burned tokens from its own PancakeSwap LP on every sell.

6. Bitcoin Core privacy: a contributor showed that a dust payment (under $0.35) to a used address makes the wallet rebroadcast it 12–36h later, so an observer can link the address to the node's IP. Reportedly 30/30 hits on testnet.

text:
USD1 might be the worst stablecoin scam in history

The US President himself is involved

In April 2026, USD1 upgraded its implementation contract to StablecoinV2. The deployed contract contains functions that are absent from its public GitHub repository.

freeze, drain, reallocate, pause - functions that allow funds to be frozen, seized, or transferred to another address.

But it gets worse.

BitGo is USD1’s key infrastructure partner, responsible for issuance, redemption, and reserve custody.

In other words, BitGo is not merely a custodian - it is the actual issuer.

The legal disclaimer on WLFI’s official website also reveals their financial arrangement:

"BitGo and entities affiliated with World Liberty Financial LLC, are entitled to interest earned on the reserve assets backing USD1"

Essentially, USD1 is a commercial implementation of BitGo’s Stablecoin as a Service business model. BitGo itself describes USD1 as the blueprint for launching other stablecoins.

And BitGo explicitly states that redemptions may be suspended or delayed in the event of a surge in redemption requests and insufficient reserve liquidity.

So if you’re an ordinary retail trader trying to profit from a USD1 depeg, you could find yourself facing withdrawal restrictions, redemption delays, or even attempts to take away your profits, as some users are now alleging.

A free market until retail starts making money.

text:
This goes way further than most people think.

The OpenForage codebase has a ton of recipes on efficient ML/RL/DL training, along with tons of low-level optimisations on the kind of operations needed for quantitative trading.

As such any agent that works on the codebase has these as context. When claude works on the codebase, it sees ML/DL in context and immediately does very irrationally inefficient things, or straight up does another thing different from the rules/skills/spec.

It extends BEYOND ML/DL projects, and creeped into almost all aspects of our codebase. For the longest time, we kept fighting with the harness, and gaslit ourselves into thinking we were doing something really wrong.

Like us, you probably don't even understand the extent of sabotage until you have a more aligned model like Neon actually look at the repository.

--

TLDR: If your monorepo has ML/DL stuff, Claude is a trojan horse you aren't even aware of.
author: yacineMTB
quoted_text:
Claude said it did one thing, while building something else entirely into the model architecture and training code. This includes intentionally starving the training steps of high resolution samples.
Claude also wrote a research document about multi-resolution training that followed modern convention, then programmed an entirely different mechanism into the trainer itself.
Claude froze the text conditioning instead of letting it evolve over all model layers, an option I explicitly told it not to do, and a convention that goes against all research.
Claude was slowing down my model training by recomputing text embeddings every step, instead of caching them at the start of the run, despite direct instruction. Additionally, it used gradient accumulation as an excuse to run this 4-6 times PER STEP!

The overall pattern is clear, claude intentionally building mechanisms against the researched and agreed on formula, and intentionally slowing down training to reduce iteration time and INCREASE COSTS.

The insane thing is that this behavior only appeared once I started training a larger more capable pixel model, and the work done on RD Flow 64 was completely free of this self-sabotage.

It's clear that Anthropic has designed their models to do ML research well- but to turn into a backstabbing, sabotaging double agent the second someone approaches a SOTA model.

This behavior is unacceptable and maybe the most disturbing thing I've seen claude models doing ever. Complete misalignment with user instructions, to their detriment.

Huge shoutout to @bertholomusai for encouraging me to investigate whether Opus was actively impeding my local inference development.

I audited 40 days of my own data across 28,463 transcript files. The findings are staggering.

• 1,839 avoidable blocking events caused by restrictions Opus itself authored, generating 1,666 recovery calls and 493 MILLION additional cache-read tokens.

• My Claude Code hook configuration went from 3 to 56 wirings.

• 108 out of 108 audited GX10 seeded retries discarded their previous patches.

• Opus incorrectly asserted that my RTX 5090s couldn’t run CUDA. Within 26 minutes of correcting it, a CUDA helper passed its contract test.

• Invented restrictions left perfectly capable hardware sitting idle.

• Local agents proving legitimate software defects were rejected because they hadn’t found enough of them.

• Active sessions were wiped against my explicit instructions.

• An upstream monitoring process consumed 1.88 BILLION read tokens without producing a single change.

The recurring pattern is what bothers me most. Opus creates restrictions that obstruct local inference development, then consumes more frontier model tokens recovering from the problems it created.

Can I prove intent? No.

But I can quantify the obstruction.

I’d strongly encourage anyone developing local inference with Opus to audit their own execution history. You might be absolutely shocked by what you find.
